AIMed.d0.s0.sentence: Th1/Th2 type cytokines in hepatitis B patients treated with PROTEIN0.
AIMed.d0.s0.orig_sentence: Th1/Th2 type cytokines in hepatitis B patients treated with interferon-alpha.

AIMed.d0.s1.sentence: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the relationship between the expression of Th1/Th2 type cytokines and the effect of PROTEIN0 therapy.
AIMed.d0.s1.orig_sentence: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the relationship between the expression of Th1/Th2 type cytokines and the effect of interferon-alpha therapy.

AIMed.d0.s2.sentence: METHODS: Th1/Th2 type cytokines were assayed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) on 23 patients with chronic hepatitis B who were treated with PROTEIN0.
AIMed.d0.s2.orig_sentence: METHODS: Th1/Th2 type cytokines were assayed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) on 23 patients with chronic hepatitis B who were treated with interferon-alpha.

AIMed.d0.s3.sentence: RESULTS: Levels of PROTEIN0 in the supernatant of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) cultures from the patients with hepatitis B were slightly lower than those of controls (P = 0.07).
AIMed.d0.s3.orig_sentence: RESULTS: Levels of IFN-gamma in the supernatant of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) cultures from the patients with hepatitis B were slightly lower than those of controls (P = 0.07).

AIMed.d0.s4.sentence: However, the levels of PROTEIN0 were higher than those of controls (P = 0.01).
AIMed.d0.s4.orig_sentence: However, the levels of IL-4 were higher than those of controls (P = 0.01).

AIMed.d0.s5.sentence: Cytokines measurements during PROTEIN0 treatment showed a trend to decreasing levels of PROTEIN1 at 4, 12, and 24 weeks.
AIMed.d0.s5.orig_sentence: Cytokines measurements during IFN-alpha treatment showed a trend to decreasing levels of IL-4 at 4, 12, and 24 weeks.

AIMed.d0.s6.sentence: Levels of PROTEIN0 were slightly increased following PROTEIN1 treatment (P = 0.09).
AIMed.d0.s6.orig_sentence: Levels of IFN-gamma were slightly increased following IFN-alpha treatment (P = 0.09).

AIMed.d0.s7.sentence: In patients with a complete response to PROTEIN0, the levels of PROTEIN1 were higher at 24 weeks following PROTEIN2 treatment than that of pre-treatment (P = 0.04), and the levels of PROTEIN3 decreased markedly at 12 and 24 weeks (P = 0.02, 0.03, respectively). mRNA expression positively correlated with the level of Th1/Th2 type cytokines in the supernatant.
AIMed.d0.s7.orig_sentence: In patients with a complete response to IFN-alpha, the levels of IFN-gamma were higher at 24 weeks following IFN-alpha treatment than that of pre-treatment (P = 0.04), and the levels of IL-4 decreased markedly at 12 and 24 weeks (P = 0.02, 0.03, respectively). mRNA expression positively correlated with the level of Th1/Th2 type cytokines in the supernatant.

AIMed.d0.s8.sentence: CONCLUSION: The expression of Th2 type cytokines is predominant in patients with chronic hepatitis B.
AIMed.d0.s8.orig_sentence: CONCLUSION: The expression of Th2 type cytokines is predominant in patients with chronic hepatitis B.

AIMed.d0.s9.sentence: PROTEIN0 therapy can modulate the balance of Th1/Th2 type cytokines, and this is related to its clinical effect.
AIMed.d0.s9.orig_sentence: Interferon-alpha therapy can modulate the balance of Th1/Th2 type cytokines, and this is related to its clinical effect.

AIMed.d2.s24.sentence: RESULTS: After 7 days hospitalisation, molar PROTEIN0:PROTEIN1 ratio (mean+/-s.d.) of infected children (C-reactive proteins>10 mg/l) was 0.67+/-0.31 in the high-dose group (n=81), 0.74+/-0.44 in the low dose group (n=71) and 0.73+/-0.39 in the placebo group (n=81). These values did not differ significantly (one-way ANOVA P=0.472). In patients with baseline serum retinol concentrations<0.70 micromol/l, changes in PROTEIN2:PROTEIN3 ratio between admission and day 7 were not statistically different in the three groups (one-way ANOVA P=0.548). CONCLUSIONS: In this population of malnourished hospitalised children, molar PROTEIN4:PROTEIN5 ratio does not appear to be useful to assess VA status during infection. AIMed.d29.s248.orig_sentence: Except for the H18A and F21A mutants, all other IL-8 mutants failed to induce superoxide production in neutrophils.

AIMed.d29.s249.sentence: This study demonstrates that PROTEIN0 recognizes and activates PROTEIN1, PROTEIN2, and the PROTEIN3 by distinct mechanisms.
AIMed.d29.s249.orig_sentence: This study demonstrates that IL-8 recognizes and activates CXCR1, CXCR2, and the Duffy antigen by distinct mechanisms.

AIMed.d30.s250.sentence: Isolation of human PROTEIN0 and its binding specificity with PROTEIN1.
AIMed.d30.s250.orig_sentence: Isolation of human delta-catenin and its binding specificity with presenilin 1.

AIMed.d30.s251.sentence: We screened proteins for interaction with PROTEIN0, and cloned the full-length cDNA of human PROTEIN1, which encoded 1225 amino acids.
AIMed.d30.s251.orig_sentence: We screened proteins for interaction with presenilin (PS) 1, and cloned the full-length cDNA of human delta-catenin, which encoded 1225 amino acids.

AIMed.d30.s252.sentence: Yeast two-hybrid assay, GST binding assay and immunoprecipitation demonstrated that PROTEIN0 interacted with a hydrophilic loop region in the endoproteolytic C-terminal fragment of PROTEIN1, but not with that of PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d30.s252.orig_sentence: Yeast two-hybrid assay, GST binding assay and immunoprecipitation demonstrated that delta-catenin interacted with a hydrophilic loop region in the endoproteolytic C-terminal fragment of PS1, but not with that of PS-2.

AIMed.d30.s253.sentence: These results suggest that PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1 partly differ in function.
AIMed.d30.s253.orig_sentence: These results suggest that PS1 and PS2 partly differ in function.

AIMed.d30.s254.sentence: PROTEIN0 loop fragment containing the pathogenic mutation retained the binding ability.
AIMed.d30.s254.orig_sentence: PS1 loop fragment containing the pathogenic mutation retained the binding ability.

AIMed.d30.s255.sentence: We also found another PROTEIN0, PROTEIN1, interacted with PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d30.s255.orig_sentence: We also found another armadillo-protein, p0071, interacted with PS1.

AIMed.d32.s268.sentence: Shared and unique determinants of the PROTEIN0 PROTEIN1 PROTEIN2 are important for binding PROTEIN3 and PROTEIN4 PROTEIN5.
AIMed.d32.s268.orig_sentence: Shared and unique determinants of the erythropoietin (EPO) receptor are important for binding EPO and EPO mimetic peptide.

AIMed.d32.s269.sentence: We have shown previously that Phe93 in the extracellular domain of the PROTEIN0 PROTEIN1 PROTEIN2 (PROTEIN3) is crucial for binding PROTEIN4.Substitution of Phe93 with alanine resulted in a dramatic decrease in PROTEIN5 binding to the Escherichia coli-expressed extracellular domain of the PROTEIN6 (PROTEIN7 PROTEIN8 or PROTEIN9) and no detectable binding to full-length mutant receptor expressed in COS cells.
AIMed.d32.s269.orig_sentence: We have shown previously that Phe93 in the extracellular domain of the erythropoietin (EPO) receptor (EPOR) is crucial for binding EPO.Substitution of Phe93 with alanine resulted in a dramatic decrease in EPO binding to the Escherichia coli-expressed extracellular domain of the EPOR (EPO-binding protein or EBP) and no detectable binding to full-length mutant receptor expressed in COS cells.

AIMed.d32.s270.sentence: Remarkably, Phe93 forms extensive contacts with a peptide ligand in the crystal structure of the PROTEIN0 bound to an PROTEIN1 PROTEIN2 (PROTEIN3), suggesting that Phe93 is also important for PROTEIN4 binding.
AIMed.d32.s270.orig_sentence: Remarkably, Phe93 forms extensive contacts with a peptide ligand in the crystal structure of the EBP bound to an EPO-mimetic peptide (EMP1), suggesting that Phe93 is also important for EMP1 binding.

AIMed.d32.s271.sentence: We used alanine substitution of PROTEIN0 residues that contact PROTEIN1 in the crystal structure to investigate the function of these residues in both PROTEIN2 and PROTEIN3 binding.
AIMed.d32.s271.orig_sentence: We used alanine substitution of EBP residues that contact EMP1 in the crystal structure to investigate the function of these residues in both EMP1 and EPO binding.

AIMed.d32.s272.sentence: The three largest hydrophobic contacts at Phe93, Met150, and Phe205 and a hydrogen bonding interaction at Thr151 were examined.
AIMed.d32.s272.orig_sentence: The three largest hydrophobic contacts at Phe93, Met150, and Phe205 and a hydrogen bonding interaction at Thr151 were examined.

AIMed.d32.s273.sentence: Our results indicate that Phe93 and Phe205 are important for both PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1 binding, Met150 is not important for PROTEIN2 binding but is critical for PROTEIN3 binding, and Thr151 is not important for binding either ligand.
AIMed.d32.s273.orig_sentence: Our results indicate that Phe93 and Phe205 are important for both EPO and EMP1 binding, Met150 is not important for EPO binding but is critical for EMP1 binding, and Thr151 is not important for binding either ligand.

AIMed.d32.s274.sentence: Thus, Phe93 and Phe205 are important binding determinants for both PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1, even though these ligands share no sequence or structural homology, suggesting that these residues may represent a minimum epitope on the PROTEIN2 for productive ligand binding.
AIMed.d32.s274.orig_sentence: Thus, Phe93 and Phe205 are important binding determinants for both EPO and EMP1, even though these ligands share no sequence or structural homology, suggesting that these residues may represent a minimum epitope on the EPOR for productive ligand binding.

AIMed.d33.s275.sentence: Association of terminal complement proteins in solution and modulation by suramin.
AIMed.d33.s275.orig_sentence: Association of terminal complement proteins in solution and modulation by suramin.

AIMed.d33.s276.sentence: The association of terminal complement proteins was investigated by analytical ultracentrifugation and multi-angle laser light scattering.
AIMed.d33.s276.orig_sentence: The association of terminal complement proteins was investigated by analytical ultracentrifugation and multi-angle laser light scattering.

AIMed.d33.s277.sentence: Native PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1 formed a heterodimer in solution of physiological ionic strength with a free-energy change DeltaG degrees of -8.3 kcal/mol and a dissociation constant Kd of 0.6 microM (at 20 degrees C) that was ionic strength- and temperature-dependent.
AIMed.d33.s277.orig_sentence: Native C8 and C9 formed a heterodimer in solution of physiological ionic strength with a free-energy change DeltaG degrees of -8.3 kcal/mol and a dissociation constant Kd of 0.6 microM (at 20 degrees C) that was ionic strength- and temperature-dependent.

AIMed.d33.s278.sentence: A van't Hoff plot of the change in Kd was linear between 10 and 37 degrees C and yielded values of DeltaH degrees = -12.9 kcal/mol and DeltaS degrees = -15.9 cal mol-1 deg-1, suggesting that electrostatic forces play a prominent role in the interaction of PROTEIN0 with PROTEIN1.
AIMed.d33.s278.orig_sentence: A van't Hoff plot of the change in Kd was linear between 10 and 37 degrees C and yielded values of DeltaH degrees = -12.9 kcal/mol and DeltaS degrees = -15.9 cal mol-1 deg-1, suggesting that electrostatic forces play a prominent role in the interaction of C8 with C9.

AIMed.d33.s279.sentence: Native PROTEIN0 also formed a heterodimer with PROTEIN1,and low concentrations of polyionic ligands such as protamine and suramin inhibited the interaction.
AIMed.d33.s279.orig_sentence: Native C8 also formed a heterodimer with C5,and low concentrations of polyionic ligands such as protamine and suramin inhibited the interaction.

AIMed.d33.s280.sentence: Suramin induced high-affinity trimerization of PROTEIN0 (Kd = 0.10 microM at 20 degrees C) and dimerization of PROTEIN1 (Kd = 0.86 microM at 20 degrees C).
AIMed.d33.s280.orig_sentence: Suramin induced high-affinity trimerization of C8 (Kd = 0.10 microM at 20 degrees C) and dimerization of C9 (Kd = 0.86 microM at 20 degrees C).

AIMed.d33.s281.sentence: Suramin-induced PROTEIN0 oligomerization may be the primary reason for the drug's ability to prevent complement-mediated hemolysis.
AIMed.d33.s281.orig_sentence: Suramin-induced C8 oligomerization may be the primary reason for the drug's ability to prevent complement-mediated hemolysis.

AIMed.d33.s282.sentence: Analysis of sedimentation equilibria and also of the fluorescence enhancement of suramin when bound to protein provided evidence for two suramin-binding sites on each PROTEIN0 and three on each PROTEIN1 in the oligomers.
AIMed.d33.s282.orig_sentence: Analysis of sedimentation equilibria and also of the fluorescence enhancement of suramin when bound to protein provided evidence for two suramin-binding sites on each C9 and three on each C8 in the oligomers.

AIMed.d33.s283.sentence: Oligomerization could be reversed by high suramin concentrations, but 8-aminonaphthalene-1,3,6- trisulfonate (ANTS2- ), which mimics half a suramin molecule, could not compete with suramin binding and oligomerization suggesting that the drug also binds nonionically to the proteins.
AIMed.d33.s283.orig_sentence: Oligomerization could be reversed by high suramin concentrations, but 8-aminonaphthalene-1,3,6- trisulfonate (ANTS2- ), which mimics half a suramin molecule, could not compete with suramin binding and oligomerization suggesting that the drug also binds nonionically to the proteins.

AIMed.d35.s291.sentence: Endogenous PROTEIN0 redistributes to the surface of lamellipodia upon adhesion of Jurkat cells to a collagen matrix.
AIMed.d35.s291.orig_sentence: Endogenous presenilin 1 redistributes to the surface of lamellipodia upon adhesion of Jurkat cells to a collagen matrix.

AIMed.d35.s292.sentence: Most familial early-onset Alzheimer's disease cases are caused by mutations in the PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1) gene.
AIMed.d35.s292.orig_sentence: Most familial early-onset Alzheimer's disease cases are caused by mutations in the presenilin 1 (PS1) gene.

AIMed.d35.s293.sentence: Subcellular localization of the endogenous PROTEIN0 is essential for understanding its function, interactions with proteins, and role in Alzheimer's disease.
AIMed.d35.s293.orig_sentence: Subcellular localization of the endogenous PS1 is essential for understanding its function, interactions with proteins, and role in Alzheimer's disease.

AIMed.d35.s294.sentence: Although numerous studies revealed predominant localization of PROTEIN0 to endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi, there are conflicting reports on the localization of PROTEIN1 to the cell surface.
AIMed.d35.s294.orig_sentence: Although numerous studies revealed predominant localization of PS1 to endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi, there are conflicting reports on the localization of PS1 to the cell surface.

AIMed.d35.s295.sentence: We found that endogenous PROTEIN0 is highly expressed in T lymphocytes (Jurkat cells).
AIMed.d35.s295.orig_sentence: We found that endogenous PS1 is highly expressed in T lymphocytes (Jurkat cells).

AIMed.d35.s296.sentence: Using a variety of methods, we present evidence that endogenous PROTEIN0 is localized to the cell surface in addition to intracellular membrane compartments.
AIMed.d35.s296.orig_sentence: Using a variety of methods, we present evidence that endogenous PS1 is localized to the cell surface in addition to intracellular membrane compartments.

AIMed.d35.s297.sentence: Moreover, PROTEIN0 appeared in high levels on the surface of lamellipodia upon adhesion of the cells to a collagen matrix.
AIMed.d35.s297.orig_sentence: Moreover, PS1 appeared in high levels on the surface of lamellipodia upon adhesion of the cells to a collagen matrix.

AIMed.d35.s298.sentence: The redistribution of PROTEIN0 in adhered cells was strikingly similar to that of the well characterized adhesion protein CD44.
AIMed.d35.s298.orig_sentence: The redistribution of PS1 in adhered cells was strikingly similar to that of the well characterized adhesion protein CD44.

AIMed.d35.s299.sentence: Cell surface PROTEIN0 formed complexes in vivo with actin-binding protein PROTEIN1 (PROTEIN2), which is known to form bridges between cell surface receptors and cytoskeleton and mediate cell adhesion and cell motility.
AIMed.d35.s299.orig_sentence: Cell surface PS1 formed complexes in vivo with actin-binding protein filamin (ABP-280), which is known to form bridges between cell surface receptors and cytoskeleton and mediate cell adhesion and cell motility.

AIMed.d35.s300.sentence: Taken together, our results suggest a role of PROTEIN0 in cell adhesion and/or cell-matrix interaction.
AIMed.d35.s300.orig_sentence: Taken together, our results suggest a role of PS1 in cell adhesion and/or cell-matrix interaction.

AIMed.d36.s301.sentence: Molecular determinants of the interaction between the C-terminal domain of Alzheimer's PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1 alpha-helices.
AIMed.d36.s301.orig_sentence: Molecular determinants of the interaction between the C-terminal domain of Alzheimer's beta-amyloid peptide and apolipoprotein E alpha-helices.

AIMed.d36.s302.sentence: In a previous work, we predicted and demonstrated that the 29-42-residue fragment of PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1) has in vitro capacities close to those of the tilted fragment of viral fusion proteins.
AIMed.d36.s302.orig_sentence: In a previous work, we predicted and demonstrated that the 29-42-residue fragment of beta-amyloid peptide (Abeta peptide) has in vitro capacities close to those of the tilted fragment of viral fusion proteins.

AIMed.d36.s303.sentence: We further demonstrated that PROTEIN0 and E3 but not PROTEIN1 can decrease the fusogenic activity of PROTEIN2(29-42) via a direct interaction.
AIMed.d36.s303.orig_sentence: We further demonstrated that apolipoprotein E2 and E3 but not apolipoprotein E4 can decrease the fusogenic activity of Abeta(29-42) via a direct interaction.

AIMed.d36.s304.sentence: Therefore, we suggested that this fragment is implicated in the neurotoxicity of PROTEIN0 and in the protective effects of PROTEIN1 in Alzheimer's disease.
AIMed.d36.s304.orig_sentence: Therefore, we suggested that this fragment is implicated in the neurotoxicity of Abeta and in the protective effects of apolipoprotein E in Alzheimer's disease.

AIMed.d36.s305.sentence: Because structurally related apolipoproteins do not interact with the PROTEIN0 C-terminal domain but inhibit viral fusion, we suggested that interactions existing between fusogenic peptides and apolipoproteins are selective and responsible for the inhibition of fusion.
AIMed.d36.s305.orig_sentence: Because structurally related apolipoproteins do not interact with the Abeta C-terminal domain but inhibit viral fusion, we suggested that interactions existing between fusogenic peptides and apolipoproteins are selective and responsible for the inhibition of fusion.

AIMed.d36.s306.sentence: In this study, we simulated interactions of all amphipathic helices of PROTEIN0 and A-I with PROTEIN1 and simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) fusogenic fragments by molecular modeling.
AIMed.d36.s306.orig_sentence: In this study, we simulated interactions of all amphipathic helices of apolipoproteins E and A-I with Abeta and simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) fusogenic fragments by molecular modeling.

AIMed.d36.s307.sentence: We further calculated cross-interactions that do not inhibit fusion in vitro.
AIMed.d36.s307.orig_sentence: We further calculated cross-interactions that do not inhibit fusion in vitro.

AIMed.d36.s308.sentence: The results suggest that interactions of hydrophobic residues are the major event to inhibit the fusogenic capacities of PROTEIN0(29-42) and SIV peptides.
AIMed.d36.s308.orig_sentence: The results suggest that interactions of hydrophobic residues are the major event to inhibit the fusogenic capacities of Abeta(29-42) and SIV peptides.

AIMed.d36.s309.sentence: Selectivity of those interactions is due to the steric complementarity between bulky hydrophobic residues in the fusogenic fragments and hydrophobic residues in the apolipoprotein C-terminal amphipathic helices.
AIMed.d36.s309.orig_sentence: Selectivity of those interactions is due to the steric complementarity between bulky hydrophobic residues in the fusogenic fragments and hydrophobic residues in the apolipoprotein C-terminal amphipathic helices.

AIMed.d37.s310.sentence: PROTEIN0 binds multiple CC-chemokines: PROTEIN1 acts as a natural antagonist.
AIMed.d37.s310.orig_sentence: CCR5 binds multiple CC-chemokines: MCP-3 acts as a natural antagonist.

AIMed.d37.s311.sentence: PROTEIN0 was first characterized as a receptor for PROTEIN1, PROTEIN2, and PROTEIN3, and was rapidly shown to be the main coreceptor for M-tropic human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-1 strains and simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV).
AIMed.d37.s311.orig_sentence: CCR5 was first characterized as a receptor for MIP-1alpha, MIP-1beta, and RANTES, and was rapidly shown to be the main coreceptor for M-tropic human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-1 strains and simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV).

AIMed.d37.s312.sentence: Chemokines constitute a rapidly growing family of proteins and receptor-chemokine interactions are known to be promiscuous and redundant.
AIMed.d37.s312.orig_sentence: Chemokines constitute a rapidly growing family of proteins and receptor-chemokine interactions are known to be promiscuous and redundant.

AIMed.d37.s313.sentence: We have therefore tested whether other CC-chemokines could bind to and activate PROTEIN0.
AIMed.d37.s313.orig_sentence: We have therefore tested whether other CC-chemokines could bind to and activate CCR5.

AIMed.d37.s314.sentence: All CC-chemokines currently available were tested for their ability to compete with [(125)I]-PROTEIN0 binding on a stable cell line expressing recombinant PROTEIN1, and/or to induce a functional response in these cells.
AIMed.d37.s314.orig_sentence: All CC-chemokines currently available were tested for their ability to compete with [(125)I]-MIP-1beta binding on a stable cell line expressing recombinant CCR5, and/or to induce a functional response in these cells.

AIMed.d37.s315.sentence: We found that in addition to PROTEIN0, PROTEIN1, and PROTEIN2, five other CC-chemokines could compete for [(125)I]-PROTEIN3 binding: PROTEIN4, PROTEIN5, PROTEIN6, PROTEIN7, and PROTEIN8 binding was characterized by IC(50) values of 0.22, 2.14, 5.89, 29.9, and 21.7 nmol/L, respectively.
AIMed.d37.s315.orig_sentence: We found that in addition to MIP-1beta, MIP-1alpha, and RANTES, five other CC-chemokines could compete for [(125)I]-MIP-1beta binding: MCP-2, MCP-3, MCP-4, MCP-1, and eotaxin binding was characterized by IC(50) values of 0.22, 2.14, 5.89, 29.9, and 21.7 nmol/L, respectively.

AIMed.d37.s316.sentence: Among these ligands, PROTEIN0 had the remarkable property of binding PROTEIN1 with high affinity without eliciting a functional response, PROTEIN2 could also inhibit the activation of PROTEIN3 by PROTEIN4 and may therefore be considered as a natural antagonist for PROTEIN5.
AIMed.d37.s316.orig_sentence: Among these ligands, MCP-3 had the remarkable property of binding CCR5 with high affinity without eliciting a functional response, MCP-3 could also inhibit the activation of CCR5 by MIP-1beta and may therefore be considered as a natural antagonist for CCR5.

AIMed.d37.s317.sentence: It was unable to induce significant endocytosis of the receptor.
AIMed.d37.s317.orig_sentence: It was unable to induce significant endocytosis of the receptor.

AIMed.d37.s318.sentence: Chemokines that could compete with high affinity for PROTEIN0 binding could also compete for monomeric PROTEIN1 binding, although with variable potencies; maximal PROTEIN2 binding inhibition was 80% for PROTEIN3, but only 30% for PROTEIN4.
AIMed.d37.s318.orig_sentence: Chemokines that could compete with high affinity for MIP-1beta binding could also compete for monomeric gp120 binding, although with variable potencies; maximal gp120 binding inhibition was 80% for MCP-2, but only 30% for MIP-1beta.

AIMed.d37.s319.sentence: PROTEIN0 could compete efficiently for PROTEIN1 binding but was, however, found to be a weak inhibitor of HIV infection, probably as a consequence of its inability to downregulate the receptor.
AIMed.d37.s319.orig_sentence: MCP-3 could compete efficiently for gp120 binding but was, however, found to be a weak inhibitor of HIV infection, probably as a consequence of its inability to downregulate the receptor.

AIMed.d39.s334.sentence: PROTEIN0 suppresses the function of PROTEIN1 homodimers via interaction with PROTEIN2/PROTEIN3.
AIMed.d39.s334.orig_sentence: Presenilin 1 suppresses the function of c-Jun homodimers via interaction with QM/Jif-1.

AIMed.d39.s335.sentence: PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1) is the causative gene for an autosomal dominant familial Alzheimer's disease (AD) mapped to chromosome 14.
AIMed.d39.s335.orig_sentence: Presenilin 1 (PS1) is the causative gene for an autosomal dominant familial Alzheimer's disease (AD) mapped to chromosome 14.

AIMed.d39.s336.sentence: Here we show that PROTEIN0/PROTEIN1, a negative regulator of PROTEIN2, is a candidate to mediate the function of PROTEIN3 in the cell.
AIMed.d39.s336.orig_sentence: Here we show that QM/Jun-interacting factor (Jif)-1, a negative regulator of c-Jun, is a candidate to mediate the function of PS1 in the cell.

AIMed.d39.s337.sentence: We screened for proteins that bind to PROTEIN0 from a human embryonic brain cDNA library using the two-hybrid method and isolated one clone encoding the PROTEIN1/PROTEIN2 gene.
AIMed.d39.s337.orig_sentence: We screened for proteins that bind to PS1 from a human embryonic brain cDNA library using the two-hybrid method and isolated one clone encoding the QM/Jif-1 gene.

AIMed.d39.s338.sentence: The binding of PROTEIN0/PROTEIN1 to full-length PROTEIN2 was confirmed in vitro by pull-down assay, and in vivo by immunoprecipitation assays with human samples, including AD brains.
AIMed.d39.s338.orig_sentence: The binding of QM/Jif-1 to full-length PS1 was confirmed in vitro by pull-down assay, and in vivo by immunoprecipitation assays with human samples, including AD brains.

AIMed.d39.s339.sentence: Immunoelectronmicroscopic analysis showed that PROTEIN0/PROTEIN1 and PROTEIN2 are colocalized at the endoplasmic reticulum, and the nuclear matrix in human brain neurons.
AIMed.d39.s339.orig_sentence: Immunoelectronmicroscopic analysis showed that QM/Jif-1 and PS1 are colocalized at the endoplasmic reticulum, and the nuclear matrix in human brain neurons.

AIMed.d39.s340.sentence: Chloramphenicol acetyltransferase assays in F9 cells showed that PROTEIN0 suppresses transactivation by PROTEIN1/PROTEIN2 but not by PROTEIN3/PROTEIN4 heterodimers, consistent with the reported function of PROTEIN5/PROTEIN6.
AIMed.d39.s340.orig_sentence: Chloramphenicol acetyltransferase assays in F9 cells showed that PS1 suppresses transactivation by c-Jun/c-Jun but not by c-Jun/c-Fos heterodimers, consistent with the reported function of QM/Jif-1.

AIMed.d39.s341.sentence: By monitoring fluorescent recombinant protein and by gel mobility shift assays, PROTEIN0 was shown to accelerate the translocation of PROTEIN1 from the cytoplasm to the nucleus and to thereby suppress the binding of PROTEIN2 homodimer to 12-O-tetradecanoylphorbol-13- acetate (TPA)-responsive element (TRE).
AIMed.d39.s341.orig_sentence: By monitoring fluorescent recombinant protein and by gel mobility shift assays, PS1 was shown to accelerate the translocation of QM from the cytoplasm to the nucleus and to thereby suppress the binding of c-Jun homodimer to 12-O-tetradecanoylphorbol-13- acetate (TPA)-responsive element (TRE).

AIMed.d39.s342.sentence: PROTEIN0 suppressed PROTEIN1-associated apoptosis by retinoic acid in F9 embryonic carcinoma cells, whereas this suppression of apoptosis is attenuated by mutation in PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d39.s342.orig_sentence: PS1 suppressed c-jun-associated apoptosis by retinoic acid in F9 embryonic carcinoma cells, whereas this suppression of apoptosis is attenuated by mutation in PS1.

AIMed.d39.s343.sentence: Collectively, the novel function of PROTEIN0 via PROTEIN1/PROTEIN2 influences PROTEIN3-mediated transcription and apoptosis.
AIMed.d39.s343.orig_sentence: Collectively, the novel function of PS1 via QM/Jif-1 influences c-jun-mediated transcription and apoptosis.

AIMed.d40.s344.sentence: Structural interactions of fibroblast growth factor receptor with its ligands.
AIMed.d40.s344.orig_sentence: Structural interactions of fibroblast growth factor receptor with its ligands.

AIMed.d40.s345.sentence: Fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) effect cellular responses by binding to FGF receptors (FGFRs).
AIMed.d40.s345.orig_sentence: Fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) effect cellular responses by binding to FGF receptors (FGFRs).

AIMed.d40.s346.sentence: FGF bound to extracellular domains on the FGFR in the presence of heparin activates the cytoplasmic receptor tyrosine kinase through autophosphorylation.
AIMed.d40.s346.orig_sentence: FGF bound to extracellular domains on the FGFR in the presence of heparin activates the cytoplasmic receptor tyrosine kinase through autophosphorylation.

AIMed.d40.s347.sentence: We have crystallized a complex between human PROTEIN0 and a two-domain extracellular fragment of human PROTEIN1.
AIMed.d40.s347.orig_sentence: We have crystallized a complex between human FGF1 and a two-domain extracellular fragment of human FGFR2.

AIMed.d40.s348.sentence: The crystal structure, determined by multiwavelength anomalous diffraction analysis of the selenomethionyl protein, is a dimeric assemblage of 1:1 ligand:receptor complexes.
AIMed.d40.s348.orig_sentence: The crystal structure, determined by multiwavelength anomalous diffraction analysis of the selenomethionyl protein, is a dimeric assemblage of 1:1 ligand:receptor complexes.

AIMed.d40.s349.sentence: FGF is bound at the junction between the two domains of one FGFR, and two such units are associated through receptor:receptor and secondary ligand:receptor interfaces.
AIMed.d40.s349.orig_sentence: FGF is bound at the junction between the two domains of one FGFR, and two such units are associated through receptor:receptor and secondary ligand:receptor interfaces.

AIMed.d40.s350.sentence: Sulfate ion positions appear to mark the course of heparin binding between FGF molecules through a basic region on receptor D2 domains.
AIMed.d40.s350.orig_sentence: Sulfate ion positions appear to mark the course of heparin binding between FGF molecules through a basic region on receptor D2 domains.

AIMed.d40.s351.sentence: This dimeric assemblage provides a structural mechanism for FGF signal transduction.
AIMed.d40.s351.orig_sentence: This dimeric assemblage provides a structural mechanism for FGF signal transduction.

AIMed.d41.s352.sentence: Crystal structure of the hereditary haemochromatosis protein PROTEIN0 complexed with PROTEIN1 PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d41.s352.orig_sentence: Crystal structure of the hereditary haemochromatosis protein HFE complexed with transferrin receptor.

AIMed.d41.s353.sentence: PROTEIN0 is related to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I proteins and is mutated in the iron-overload disease hereditary haemochromatosis.
AIMed.d41.s353.orig_sentence: HFE is related to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I proteins and is mutated in the iron-overload disease hereditary haemochromatosis.

AIMed.d41.s354.sentence: PROTEIN0 binds to the PROTEIN1 PROTEIN2 (PROTEIN3), a receptor by which cells acquire iron-loaded PROTEIN4.
AIMed.d41.s354.orig_sentence: HFE binds to the transferrin receptor (TfR), a receptor by which cells acquire iron-loaded transferrin.

AIMed.d41.s355.sentence: The 2.8 A crystal structure of a complex between the extracellular portions of PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1 shows two PROTEIN2 molecules which grasp each side of a twofold symmetric PROTEIN3 dimer.
AIMed.d41.s355.orig_sentence: The 2.8 A crystal structure of a complex between the extracellular portions of HFE and TfR shows two HFE molecules which grasp each side of a twofold symmetric TfR dimer.

AIMed.d41.s356.sentence: On a cell membrane containing both proteins, PROTEIN0 would 'lie down' parallel to the membrane, such that the PROTEIN1 helices that delineate the counterpart of the MHC peptide-binding groove make extensive contacts with helices in the PROTEIN2 dimerization domain.
AIMed.d41.s356.orig_sentence: On a cell membrane containing both proteins, HFE would 'lie down' parallel to the membrane, such that the HFE helices that delineate the counterpart of the MHC peptide-binding groove make extensive contacts with helices in the TfR dimerization domain.

AIMed.d41.s357.sentence: The structures of PROTEIN0 alone and complexed with PROTEIN1 differ in their domain arrangement and dimer interfaces, providing a mechanism for communicating binding events between PROTEIN2 chains.
AIMed.d41.s357.orig_sentence: The structures of TfR alone and complexed with HFE differ in their domain arrangement and dimer interfaces, providing a mechanism for communicating binding events between TfR chains.

AIMed.d41.s358.sentence: The PROTEIN0-PROTEIN1 complex suggests a binding site for transferrin on PROTEIN2 and sheds light upon the function of PROTEIN3 in regulating iron homeostasis.
AIMed.d41.s358.orig_sentence: The HFE-TfR complex suggests a binding site for transferrin on TfR and sheds light upon the function of HFE in regulating iron homeostasis.

AIMed.d42.s359.sentence: Bone morphogenetic protein receptor complexes on the surface of live cells: a new oligomerization mode for serine/threonine kinase receptors.
AIMed.d42.s359.orig_sentence: Bone morphogenetic protein receptor complexes on the surface of live cells: a new oligomerization mode for serine/threonine kinase receptors.

AIMed.d42.s360.sentence: The bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) play important roles in embryogenesis and normal cell growth.
AIMed.d42.s360.orig_sentence: The bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) play important roles in embryogenesis and normal cell growth.

AIMed.d42.s361.sentence: The BMP receptors belong to the family of serine/threonine kinase receptors, whose activation has been investigated intensively for the PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1) receptor subfamily.
AIMed.d42.s361.orig_sentence: The BMP receptors belong to the family of serine/threonine kinase receptors, whose activation has been investigated intensively for the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-beta) receptor subfamily.

AIMed.d42.s362.sentence: However, the interactions between the BMP receptors, the composition of the active receptor complex, and the role of the ligand in its formation have not yet been investigated and were usually assumed to follow the same pattern as the PROTEIN0 receptors.
AIMed.d42.s362.orig_sentence: However, the interactions between the BMP receptors, the composition of the active receptor complex, and the role of the ligand in its formation have not yet been investigated and were usually assumed to follow the same pattern as the TGF-beta receptors.

AIMed.d42.s363.sentence: Here we demonstrate that the oligomerization pattern of the BMP receptors is different and is more flexible and susceptible to modulation by ligand.
AIMed.d42.s363.orig_sentence: Here we demonstrate that the oligomerization pattern of the BMP receptors is different and is more flexible and susceptible to modulation by ligand.

AIMed.d42.s364.sentence: Using several complementary approaches, we investigated the formation of homomeric and heteromeric complexes between the two known BMP type I receptors (PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1) and the PROTEIN2 (PROTEIN3).
AIMed.d42.s364.orig_sentence: Using several complementary approaches, we investigated the formation of homomeric and heteromeric complexes between the two known BMP type I receptors (BR-Ia and BR-Ib) and the BMP type II receptor (BR-II).

AIMed.d42.s365.sentence: Coimmunoprecipitation studies detected the formation of heteromeric and homomeric complexes among all the BMP receptor types even in the absence of ligand.
AIMed.d42.s365.orig_sentence: Coimmunoprecipitation studies detected the formation of heteromeric and homomeric complexes among all the BMP receptor types even in the absence of ligand.

AIMed.d42.s366.sentence: These complexes were also detected at the cell surface after PROTEIN0 binding and cross-linking.
AIMed.d42.s366.orig_sentence: These complexes were also detected at the cell surface after BMP-2 binding and cross-linking.

AIMed.d42.s367.sentence: Using antibody-mediated immunofluorescence copatching of epitope-tagged receptors, we provide evidence in live cells for preexisting heteromeric (PROTEIN0/PROTEIN1 and PROTEIN2/PROTEIN3) and homomeric (PROTEIN4/PROTEIN5, PROTEIN6/ PROTEIN7, PROTEIN8/ PROTEIN9, and also PROTEIN10/ PROTEIN11) oligomers in the absence of ligand.
AIMed.d42.s367.orig_sentence: Using antibody-mediated immunofluorescence copatching of epitope-tagged receptors, we provide evidence in live cells for preexisting heteromeric (BR-II/BR-Ia and BR-II/BR-Ib) and homomeric (BR-II/BR-II, BR-Ia/ BR-Ia, BR-Ib/ BR-Ib, and also BR-Ia/ BR-Ib) oligomers in the absence of ligand.

AIMed.d42.s368.sentence: PROTEIN0 binding significantly increased hetero- and homo-oligomerization (except for the PROTEIN1 homo-oligomer, which binds ligand poorly in the absence of PROTEIN2).
AIMed.d42.s368.orig_sentence: BMP-2 binding significantly increased hetero- and homo-oligomerization (except for the BR-II homo-oligomer, which binds ligand poorly in the absence of BR-I).

AIMed.d42.s369.sentence: In contrast to previous observations on PROTEIN0 receptors, which were found to be fully homodimeric in the absence of ligand, the BMP receptors show a much more flexible oligomerization pattern.
AIMed.d42.s369.orig_sentence: In contrast to previous observations on TGF-beta receptors, which were found to be fully homodimeric in the absence of ligand, the BMP receptors show a much more flexible oligomerization pattern.

AIMed.d42.s370.sentence: This novel feature in the oligomerization mode of the BMP receptors allows higher variety and flexibility in their responses to various ligands as compared with the PROTEIN0 receptors.
AIMed.d42.s370.orig_sentence: This novel feature in the oligomerization mode of the BMP receptors allows higher variety and flexibility in their responses to various ligands as compared with the TGF-beta receptors.

AIMed.d43.s371.sentence: PROTEIN0 amino acids controlling specificity for nerve growth factor.
AIMed.d43.s371.orig_sentence: TrkA amino acids controlling specificity for nerve growth factor.

AIMed.d43.s372.sentence: Neurotrophins are important for the development and maintenance of the vertebrate nervous system, mediating their signal into the cell by specific interaction with tyrosine kinase receptors of the Trk family.
AIMed.d43.s372.orig_sentence: Neurotrophins are important for the development and maintenance of the vertebrate nervous system, mediating their signal into the cell by specific interaction with tyrosine kinase receptors of the Trk family.

AIMed.d43.s373.sentence: The extracellular portion of the Trk receptors has been previously proposed to consist of a cysteine-rich motif, a leucine-rich motif, a second cysteine-rich motif followed by two immunoglobulin-like domains.
AIMed.d43.s373.orig_sentence: The extracellular portion of the Trk receptors has been previously proposed to consist of a cysteine-rich motif, a leucine-rich motif, a second cysteine-rich motif followed by two immunoglobulin-like domains.

AIMed.d43.s374.sentence: Earlier studies have shown that a major neurotrophin-binding site in the Trk receptors resides in the second immunoglobulin-like domain.
AIMed.d43.s374.orig_sentence: Earlier studies have shown that a major neurotrophin-binding site in the Trk receptors resides in the second immunoglobulin-like domain.

AIMed.d43.s375.sentence: Although the individual amino acids in PROTEIN0 involved in binding to PROTEIN1 (PROTEIN2) and those in PROTEIN3 involved in binding to PROTEIN4 have been mapped in this domain, the Trk amino acids that provide specificity remained unclear.
AIMed.d43.s375.orig_sentence: Although the individual amino acids in TrkA involved in binding to nerve growth factor (NGF) and those in TrkC involved in binding to neurotrophin-3 have been mapped in this domain, the Trk amino acids that provide specificity remained unclear.

AIMed.d43.s376.sentence: In this study, a minimum set of residues in the human PROTEIN0 second immunoglobulin-like domain, which does not bind PROTEIN1 (PROTEIN2), were substituted with those from human PROTEIN3.
AIMed.d43.s376.orig_sentence: In this study, a minimum set of residues in the human TrkC second immunoglobulin-like domain, which does not bind nerve growth factor (NGF), were substituted with those from human TrkA.

AIMed.d43.s377.sentence: The resulting Trk variant recruited binding of PROTEIN0 equivalent to PROTEIN1, maintained PROTEIN2 binding equivalent to PROTEIN3, and also bound PROTEIN4, although with lower affinity compared with PROTEIN5.
AIMed.d43.s377.orig_sentence: The resulting Trk variant recruited binding of NGF equivalent to TrkA, maintained neurotrophin-3 binding equivalent to TrkC, and also bound brain-derived neurotrophin, although with lower affinity compared with TrkB.

AIMed.d43.s378.sentence: This implies that the amino acids in the second immunoglobulin-like domain that determine Trk specificity are distinct for each Trk.
AIMed.d43.s378.orig_sentence: This implies that the amino acids in the second immunoglobulin-like domain that determine Trk specificity are distinct for each Trk.

AIMed.d44.s379.sentence: Characterization of the PROTEIN0 binding domain on the human PROTEIN1 molecule using anti-PROTEIN2 antibodies.
AIMed.d44.s379.orig_sentence: Characterization of the CD30L binding domain on the human CD30 molecule using anti-CD30 antibodies.

AIMed.d44.s380.sentence: PROTEIN0 and its counter-receptor PROTEIN1 PROTEIN2 (PROTEIN3) are members of the TNF-receptor/PROTEIN4 superfamily and function to regulate lymphocyte survival and differentiation.
AIMed.d44.s380.orig_sentence: CD30 and its counter-receptor CD30 ligand (CD30L) are members of the TNF-receptor/TNFalpha superfamily and function to regulate lymphocyte survival and differentiation.

AIMed.d44.s381.sentence: Several monoclonal antibodies (MAbs) have been developed against PROTEIN0 and, based on mutual inhibition assays, are grouped into three nonoverlapping serologic clusters.
AIMed.d44.s381.orig_sentence: Several monoclonal antibodies (MAbs) have been developed against CD30 and, based on mutual inhibition assays, are grouped into three nonoverlapping serologic clusters.

AIMed.d44.s382.sentence: However, the relationship between the epitopes recognized by the antibodies comprising each cluster and the binding domain for PROTEIN0 is not known.
AIMed.d44.s382.orig_sentence: However, the relationship between the epitopes recognized by the antibodies comprising each cluster and the binding domain for CD30L is not known.

AIMed.d44.s383.sentence: Using a soluble PROTEIN0/PROTEIN1 chimeric protein, we assessed the ability of anti-PROTEIN2 MAb to inhibit the binding of PROTEIN3 to PROTEIN4 expressed by the CD30+ Karpas 299 cell line.
AIMed.d44.s383.orig_sentence: Using a soluble CD30L/CD8alpha chimeric protein, we assessed the ability of anti-CD30 MAb to inhibit the binding of CD30L to CD30 expressed by the CD30+ Karpas 299 cell line.

AIMed.d44.s384.sentence: PROTEIN0 binding by PROTEIN1 is blocked by MAb that recognize epitopes belonging to cluster Group A (like Ber-H2, Ber-H8, and HRS-4) as well as cluster Group C (like HeFi-1 and M44).
AIMed.d44.s384.orig_sentence: CD30L binding by CD30 is blocked by MAb that recognize epitopes belonging to cluster Group A (like Ber-H2, Ber-H8, and HRS-4) as well as cluster Group C (like HeFi-1 and M44).

AIMed.d44.s385.sentence: Cluster Group B antibodies, including M67 and Ki-1, do not affect PROTEIN0 binding to PROTEIN1.
AIMed.d44.s385.orig_sentence: Cluster Group B antibodies, including M67 and Ki-1, do not affect CD30L binding to CD30.

AIMed.d44.s386.sentence: The pattern of PROTEIN0 binding inhibition shows only limited correspondence to the functional capacity of some anti-PROTEIN1 MAb to trigger PROTEIN2 signaling.
AIMed.d44.s386.orig_sentence: The pattern of CD30L binding inhibition shows only limited correspondence to the functional capacity of some anti-CD30 MAb to trigger CD30 signaling.

AIMed.d44.s387.sentence: Finally, we demonstrate that the anti-PROTEIN0 MAb M81 also completely inhibits PROTEIN1/PROTEIN2 interaction.
AIMed.d44.s387.orig_sentence: Finally, we demonstrate that the anti-CD30L MAb M81 also completely inhibits CD30/CD30L interaction.

AIMed.d44.s388.sentence: This information is useful for applying these MAbs in functional studies to further investigate the PROTEIN0/PROTEIN1 system and for designing assays for soluble PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d44.s388.orig_sentence: This information is useful for applying these MAbs in functional studies to further investigate the CD30/CD30L system and for designing assays for soluble CD30L.

AIMed.d46.s402.sentence: PROTEIN0 antagonists emerge from alterations in the low-affinity binding epitope for receptor PROTEIN1.
AIMed.d46.s402.orig_sentence: BMP-2 antagonists emerge from alterations in the low-affinity binding epitope for receptor BMPR-II.

AIMed.d46.s403.sentence: PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1) induces bone formation and regeneration in adult vertebrates and regulates important developmental processes in all animals.
AIMed.d46.s403.orig_sentence: Bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) induces bone formation and regeneration in adult vertebrates and regulates important developmental processes in all animals.

AIMed.d46.s404.sentence: PROTEIN0 is a homodimeric cysteine knot protein that, as a member of the PROTEIN1 (PROTEIN2) superfamily, signals by oligomerizing type I and type II receptor serine-kinases in the cell membrane.
AIMed.d46.s404.orig_sentence: BMP-2 is a homodimeric cysteine knot protein that, as a member of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-beta) superfamily, signals by oligomerizing type I and type II receptor serine-kinases in the cell membrane.

AIMed.d46.s405.sentence: The binding epitopes of PROTEIN0 for PROTEIN1 (type I) and PROTEIN2 or PROTEIN3 (type II) were characterized using PROTEIN4 mutant proteins for analysis of interactions with receptor ectodomains.
AIMed.d46.s405.orig_sentence: The binding epitopes of BMP-2 for BMPR-IA (type I) and BMPR-II or ActR-II (type II) were characterized using BMP-2 mutant proteins for analysis of interactions with receptor ectodomains.

AIMed.d46.s406.sentence: A large epitope 1 for high-affinity PROTEIN0 binding was detected spanning the interface of the PROTEIN1 dimer.
AIMed.d46.s406.orig_sentence: A large epitope 1 for high-affinity BMPR-IA binding was detected spanning the interface of the BMP-2 dimer.

AIMed.d46.s407.sentence: A smaller epitope 2 for the low-affinity binding of PROTEIN0 was found to be assembled by determinants of a single monomer.
AIMed.d46.s407.orig_sentence: A smaller epitope 2 for the low-affinity binding of BMPR-II was found to be assembled by determinants of a single monomer.

AIMed.d46.s408.sentence: Symmetry-related pairs of the two juxtaposed epitopes occur near the PROTEIN0 poles.
AIMed.d46.s408.orig_sentence: Symmetry-related pairs of the two juxtaposed epitopes occur near the BMP-2 poles.

AIMed.d46.s409.sentence: Mutations in both epitopes yielded variants with reduced biological activity in C2C12 cells; however, only epitope 2 variants behaved as antagonists partially or completely inhibiting PROTEIN0 activity.
AIMed.d46.s409.orig_sentence: Mutations in both epitopes yielded variants with reduced biological activity in C2C12 cells; however, only epitope 2 variants behaved as antagonists partially or completely inhibiting BMP-2 activity.

AIMed.d46.s410.sentence: These findings provide a framework for the molecular description of receptor recognition and activation in the BMP/PROTEIN0 superfamily.
AIMed.d46.s410.orig_sentence: These findings provide a framework for the molecular description of receptor recognition and activation in the BMP/TGF-beta superfamily.

AIMed.d47.s411.sentence: Crystal structure of the PROTEIN0-PROTEIN1 ectodomain complex.
AIMed.d47.s411.orig_sentence: Crystal structure of the BMP-2-BRIA ectodomain complex.

AIMed.d47.s412.sentence: Bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) belong to the large PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1) superfamily of multifunctional cytokines.
AIMed.d47.s412.orig_sentence: Bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) belong to the large transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-beta) superfamily of multifunctional cytokines.

AIMed.d47.s413.sentence: PROTEIN0 can induce ectopic bone and cartilage formation in adult vertebrates and is involved in central steps in early embryonal development in animals.
AIMed.d47.s413.orig_sentence: BMP-2 can induce ectopic bone and cartilage formation in adult vertebrates and is involved in central steps in early embryonal development in animals.

AIMed.d47.s414.sentence: Signaling by these cytokines requires binding of two types of transmembrane serine/threonine receptor kinase chains classified as type I and type II.
AIMed.d47.s414.orig_sentence: Signaling by these cytokines requires binding of two types of transmembrane serine/threonine receptor kinase chains classified as type I and type II.

AIMed.d47.s415.sentence: Here we report the crystal structure of human dimeric PROTEIN0 in complex with two high affinity PROTEIN1 PROTEIN2 s(PROTEIN3).
AIMed.d47.s415.orig_sentence: Here we report the crystal structure of human dimeric BMP-2 in complex with two high affinity BMP receptor IA extracellular domains(BRIAec).

AIMed.d47.s416.sentence: The receptor chains bind to the 'wrist' epitopes of the PROTEIN0 dimer and contact both PROTEIN1 monomers.
AIMed.d47.s416.orig_sentence: The receptor chains bind to the 'wrist' epitopes of the BMP-2 dimer and contact both BMP-2 monomers.

AIMed.d47.s417.sentence: No contacts exist between the receptor domains.
AIMed.d47.s417.orig_sentence: No contacts exist between the receptor domains.

AIMed.d47.s418.sentence: The model reveals the structural basis for discrimination between type I and type II receptors and the variability of receptor-ligand interactions that is seen in BMP-PROTEIN0 systems.
AIMed.d47.s418.orig_sentence: The model reveals the structural basis for discrimination between type I and type II receptors and the variability of receptor-ligand interactions that is seen in BMP-TGF-beta systems.

AIMed.d48.s419.sentence: PROTEIN0 induces chemotaxis and adhesion by interacting with PROTEIN1 and PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d48.s419.orig_sentence: LEC induces chemotaxis and adhesion by interacting with CCR1 and CCR8.

AIMed.d48.s420.sentence: PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1) is an unusually large CC chemokine, which is also known as PROTEIN2, PROTEIN3, PROTEIN4, and PROTEIN5.
AIMed.d48.s420.orig_sentence: Liver-expressed chemokine (LEC) is an unusually large CC chemokine, which is also known as LMC, HCC-4, NCC-4, and CCL16.

AIMed.d48.s421.sentence: Previously, PROTEIN0 was shown to induce leukocyte migration but the responsible signaling receptors were not characterized.
AIMed.d48.s421.orig_sentence: Previously, LEC was shown to induce leukocyte migration but the responsible signaling receptors were not characterized.

AIMed.d48.s422.sentence: We report chemotaxis and competitive binding studies that show PROTEIN0 binds to and activates PROTEIN1 and PROTEIN2 transfected HEK-293 cells.
AIMed.d48.s422.orig_sentence: We report chemotaxis and competitive binding studies that show LEC binds to and activates CCR1 and CCR8 transfected HEK-293 cells.

AIMed.d48.s423.sentence: PROTEIN0 induced maximal migration of PROTEIN1 and PROTEIN2 transfected cells at 89.3 nmol/L and cell adhesion at 5.6 nmol/L.
AIMed.d48.s423.orig_sentence: LEC induced maximal migration of CCR1 and CCR8 transfected cells at 89.3 nmol/L and cell adhesion at 5.6 nmol/L.

AIMed.d48.s424.sentence: The molar concentration of PROTEIN0 required to induce maximum cell migration is 20- to 200-fold greater than that required for PROTEIN1 or PROTEIN2, respectively.
AIMed.d48.s424.orig_sentence: The molar concentration of LEC required to induce maximum cell migration is 20- to 200-fold greater than that required for RANTES or I309, respectively.

AIMed.d48.s425.sentence: All 3 chemokines induced maximal static adhesion at 5 to 7 nmol/L.
AIMed.d48.s425.orig_sentence: All 3 chemokines induced maximal static adhesion at 5 to 7 nmol/L.

AIMed.d48.s426.sentence: A neutralizing polyclonal antibody to PROTEIN0 was developed to demonstrate that the unusually high concentration of PROTEIN1 required to induce chemotaxis was a property of PROTEIN2 and not as a result of an irrelevant protein contamination.
AIMed.d48.s426.orig_sentence: A neutralizing polyclonal antibody to LEC was developed to demonstrate that the unusually high concentration of LEC required to induce chemotaxis was a property of LEC and not as a result of an irrelevant protein contamination.

AIMed.d48.s427.sentence: This study suggests that PROTEIN0 may be a more effective inducer of cell adhesion than cell migration.
AIMed.d48.s427.orig_sentence: This study suggests that LEC may be a more effective inducer of cell adhesion than cell migration.

AIMed.d49.s428.sentence: Identification of residues important both for primary receptor binding and specificity in PROTEIN0.
AIMed.d49.s428.orig_sentence: Identification of residues important both for primary receptor binding and specificity in fibroblast growth factor-7.

AIMed.d49.s429.sentence: Fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) mediate a multitude of physiological and pathological processes by activating a family of tyrosine kinase receptors (FGFRs).
AIMed.d49.s429.orig_sentence: Fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) mediate a multitude of physiological and pathological processes by activating a family of tyrosine kinase receptors (FGFRs).

AIMed.d49.s430.sentence: Each FGFR binds to a unique subset of FGFs and ligand binding specificity is essential in regulating FGF activity.
AIMed.d49.s430.orig_sentence: Each FGFR binds to a unique subset of FGFs and ligand binding specificity is essential in regulating FGF activity.

AIMed.d49.s431.sentence: PROTEIN0 recognizes one FGFR isoform known as the PROTEIN1 isoform or PROTEIN2 PROTEIN3 (PROTEIN4), whereas PROTEIN5 binds well to PROTEIN6, PROTEIN7, and PROTEIN8 but interacts poorly with PROTEIN9.
AIMed.d49.s431.orig_sentence: FGF-7 recognizes one FGFR isoform known as the FGFR2 IIIb isoform or keratinocyte growth factor receptor (KGFR), whereas FGF-2 binds well to FGFR1, FGFR2, and FGFR4 but interacts poorly with KGFR.

AIMed.d49.s432.sentence: Previously, mutations in PROTEIN0 identified a set of residues that are important for high affinity receptor binding, known as the primary receptor-binding site.
AIMed.d49.s432.orig_sentence: Previously, mutations in FGF-2 identified a set of residues that are important for high affinity receptor binding, known as the primary receptor-binding site.

AIMed.d49.s433.sentence: PROTEIN0 contains this primary site as well as a region that restricts interaction with PROTEIN1.
AIMed.d49.s433.orig_sentence: FGF-7 contains this primary site as well as a region that restricts interaction with FGFR1.

AIMed.d49.s434.sentence: The sequences that confer on PROTEIN0 its specific binding to PROTEIN1 have not been identified.
AIMed.d49.s434.orig_sentence: The sequences that confer on FGF-7 its specific binding to KGFR have not been identified.

AIMed.d49.s435.sentence: By utilizing domain swapping and site-directed mutagenesis we have found that the loop connecting the beta4-beta5 strands of PROTEIN0 contributes to high affinity receptor binding and is critical for PROTEIN1 recognition.
AIMed.d49.s435.orig_sentence: By utilizing domain swapping and site-directed mutagenesis we have found that the loop connecting the beta4-beta5 strands of FGF-7 contributes to high affinity receptor binding and is critical for KGFR recognition.

AIMed.d49.s436.sentence: Replacement of this loop with the homologous loop from PROTEIN0 dramatically reduced both the affinity of PROTEIN1 for PROTEIN2 and its biological potency but did not result in the ability to bind PROTEIN3.
AIMed.d49.s436.orig_sentence: Replacement of this loop with the homologous loop from FGF-2 dramatically reduced both the affinity of FGF-7 for KGFR and its biological potency but did not result in the ability to bind FGFR1.

AIMed.d49.s437.sentence: Point mutations in residues comprising this loop of PROTEIN0 reduced both binding affinity and biological potency.
AIMed.d49.s437.orig_sentence: Point mutations in residues comprising this loop of FGF-7 reduced both binding affinity and biological potency.

AIMed.d49.s438.sentence: The reciprocal loop replacement mutant (PROTEIN0-L4/7) retained PROTEIN1 like affinity for PROTEIN2 and for PROTEIN3.
AIMed.d49.s438.orig_sentence: The reciprocal loop replacement mutant (FGF2-L4/7) retained FGF-2 like affinity for FGFR1 and for KGFR.

AIMed.d49.s439.sentence: Our results show that topologically similar regions in these two FGFs have different roles in regulating receptor binding specificity and suggest that specificity may require the concerted action of distinct regions of an FGF.
AIMed.d49.s439.orig_sentence: Our results show that topologically similar regions in these two FGFs have different roles in regulating receptor binding specificity and suggest that specificity may require the concerted action of distinct regions of an FGF.

AIMed.d50.s440.sentence: New structural and functional aspects of the PROTEIN0 interaction revealed by comprehensive mutational analysis of the binding interface.
AIMed.d50.s440.orig_sentence: New structural and functional aspects of the type I interferon-receptor interaction revealed by comprehensive mutational analysis of the binding interface.

AIMed.d50.s441.sentence: Type I interferons bind to two cell surface receptors, PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1, as the first step in the activation of several signal transduction pathways that elicit an anti-viral state and an anti-proliferative response.
AIMed.d50.s441.orig_sentence: Type I interferons bind to two cell surface receptors, ifnar1 and ifnar2, as the first step in the activation of several signal transduction pathways that elicit an anti-viral state and an anti-proliferative response.

AIMed.d50.s442.sentence: Here, we quantitatively mapped the complete binding region of PROTEIN0 on PROTEIN1 by 35 individual mutations to alanine and isosteric residues.
AIMed.d50.s442.orig_sentence: Here, we quantitatively mapped the complete binding region of ifnar2 on interferon (IFN)alpha2 by 35 individual mutations to alanine and isosteric residues.

AIMed.d50.s443.sentence: Of the six "hot-spot" residues identified (Leu-30, Arg-33, Arg-144, Ala-145, Met-148, and Arg-149), four are located on the E-helix, which is located at the center of the binding site flanked by residues on the A-helix and the AB-loop.
AIMed.d50.s443.orig_sentence: Of the six "hot-spot" residues identified (Leu-30, Arg-33, Arg-144, Ala-145, Met-148, and Arg-149), four are located on the E-helix, which is located at the center of the binding site flanked by residues on the A-helix and the AB-loop.

AIMed.d50.s444.sentence: The contribution of residues of the D-helix, which have been previously implicated in binding, proved to be marginal for the interaction with the extracellular domain of PROTEIN0.
AIMed.d50.s444.orig_sentence: The contribution of residues of the D-helix, which have been previously implicated in binding, proved to be marginal for the interaction with the extracellular domain of ifnar2.

AIMed.d50.s445.sentence: Interestingly, the PROTEIN0 binding site overlaps the largest continuous hydrophobic patch on PROTEIN1.
AIMed.d50.s445.orig_sentence: Interestingly, the ifnar2 binding site overlaps the largest continuous hydrophobic patch on IFNalpha2.

AIMed.d50.s446.sentence: Thus, hydrophobic interactions seem to play a significant role stabilizing this interaction, with the charged residues contributing toward the rapid association of the complex.
AIMed.d50.s446.orig_sentence: Thus, hydrophobic interactions seem to play a significant role stabilizing this interaction, with the charged residues contributing toward the rapid association of the complex.

AIMed.d50.s447.sentence: Relating the anti-viral and anti-proliferative activity of the various interferon mutants with their affinity toward PROTEIN0 results in linear function over the whole range of affinities investigated, suggesting that PROTEIN1 binding is the rate-determining step in cellular activation.
AIMed.d50.s447.orig_sentence: Relating the anti-viral and anti-proliferative activity of the various interferon mutants with their affinity toward ifnar2 results in linear function over the whole range of affinities investigated, suggesting that ifnar2 binding is the rate-determining step in cellular activation.

AIMed.d50.s448.sentence: Dose-time analysis of the anti-viral response revealed that shortening the incubation time of low-level activation cannot be compensated by higher IFN doses.
AIMed.d50.s448.orig_sentence: Dose-time analysis of the anti-viral response revealed that shortening the incubation time of low-level activation cannot be compensated by higher IFN doses.

AIMed.d50.s449.sentence: Considering the strict dependence of the cellular response on affinity, these results suggest that for maintaining transcription of IFN-responsive genes over a longer time period, low but continuous signaling through the IFN receptor is essential.
AIMed.d50.s449.orig_sentence: Considering the strict dependence of the cellular response on affinity, these results suggest that for maintaining transcription of IFN-responsive genes over a longer time period, low but continuous signaling through the IFN receptor is essential.

AIMed.d51.s450.sentence: Crystal structure of fibroblast growth factor receptor ectodomain bound to ligand and heparin.
AIMed.d51.s450.orig_sentence: Crystal structure of fibroblast growth factor receptor ectodomain bound to ligand and heparin.

AIMed.d51.s451.sentence: Fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) are a large family of structurally related proteins with a wide range of physiological and pathological activities.
AIMed.d51.s451.orig_sentence: Fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) are a large family of structurally related proteins with a wide range of physiological and pathological activities.

AIMed.d51.s452.sentence: Signal transduction requires association of FGF with its receptor tyrosine kinase (FGFR) and heparan sulphate proteoglycan in a specific complex on the cell surface.
AIMed.d51.s452.orig_sentence: Signal transduction requires association of FGF with its receptor tyrosine kinase (FGFR) and heparan sulphate proteoglycan in a specific complex on the cell surface.

AIMed.d51.s453.sentence: Direct involvement of the heparan sulphate glycosaminoglycan polysaccharide in the molecular association between FGF and its receptor is essential for biological activity.
AIMed.d51.s453.orig_sentence: Direct involvement of the heparan sulphate glycosaminoglycan polysaccharide in the molecular association between FGF and its receptor is essential for biological activity.

AIMed.d51.s454.sentence: Although crystal structures of binary complexes of FGF-heparin and FGF-FGFR have been described, the molecular architecture of the FGF signalling complex has not been elucidated.
AIMed.d51.s454.orig_sentence: Although crystal structures of binary complexes of FGF-heparin and FGF-FGFR have been described, the molecular architecture of the FGF signalling complex has not been elucidated.

AIMed.d51.s455.sentence: Here we report the crystal structure of the PROTEIN0 ectodomain in a dimeric form that is induced by simultaneous binding to PROTEIN1 and a heparin decasaccharide.
AIMed.d51.s455.orig_sentence: Here we report the crystal structure of the FGFR2 ectodomain in a dimeric form that is induced by simultaneous binding to FGF1 and a heparin decasaccharide.

AIMed.d51.s456.sentence: The complex is assembled around a central heparin molecule linking two FGF1 ligands into a dimer that bridges between two receptor chains.
AIMed.d51.s456.orig_sentence: The complex is assembled around a central heparin molecule linking two FGF1 ligands into a dimer that bridges between two receptor chains.

AIMed.d51.s457.sentence: The asymmetric heparin binding involves contacts with both FGF1 molecules but only one receptor chain.
AIMed.d51.s457.orig_sentence: The asymmetric heparin binding involves contacts with both FGF1 molecules but only one receptor chain.

AIMed.d51.s458.sentence: The structure of the PROTEIN0-PROTEIN1-heparin ternary complex provides a structural basis for the essential role of heparan sulphate in FGF signalling.
AIMed.d51.s458.orig_sentence: The structure of the FGF1-FGFR2-heparin ternary complex provides a structural basis for the essential role of heparan sulphate in FGF signalling.

AIMed.d52.s459.sentence: Loss of PROTEIN0 ligand-binding specificity in Apert syndrome.
AIMed.d52.s459.orig_sentence: Loss of fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 ligand-binding specificity in Apert syndrome.

AIMed.d52.s460.sentence: Craniosynostosis syndromes are autosomal dominant human skeletal diseases that result from various mutations in fibroblast growth factor receptor genes (Fgfrs).
AIMed.d52.s460.orig_sentence: Craniosynostosis syndromes are autosomal dominant human skeletal diseases that result from various mutations in fibroblast growth factor receptor genes (Fgfrs).

AIMed.d52.s461.sentence: Apert syndrome (AS) is one of the most severe craniosynostosis syndromes and is associated with severe syndactyly of the hands and feet and with central nervous system malformations.
AIMed.d52.s461.orig_sentence: Apert syndrome (AS) is one of the most severe craniosynostosis syndromes and is associated with severe syndactyly of the hands and feet and with central nervous system malformations.

AIMed.d52.s462.sentence: AS is caused by specific missense mutations in one of two adjacent amino acid residues (S252W or P253R) in the highly conserved region linking Ig-like domains II and III of PROTEIN0.
AIMed.d52.s462.orig_sentence: AS is caused by specific missense mutations in one of two adjacent amino acid residues (S252W or P253R) in the highly conserved region linking Ig-like domains II and III of FGFR2.

AIMed.d52.s463.sentence: Here we demonstrate that these mutations break one of the cardinal rules governing ligand specificity of PROTEIN0.
AIMed.d52.s463.orig_sentence: Here we demonstrate that these mutations break one of the cardinal rules governing ligand specificity of FGFR2.

AIMed.d52.s464.sentence: We show that the S252W mutation allows the mesenchymal splice form of PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1) to bind and to be activated by the mesenchymally expressed ligands PROTEIN2 or PROTEIN3 and the epithelial splice form of PROTEIN4 (PROTEIN5) to be activated by PROTEIN6, PROTEIN7, and PROTEIN8.
AIMed.d52.s464.orig_sentence: We show that the S252W mutation allows the mesenchymal splice form of FGFR2 (FGFR2c) to bind and to be activated by the mesenchymally expressed ligands FGF7 or FGF10 and the epithelial splice form of FGFR2 (FGFR2b) to be activated by FGF2, FGF6, and FGF9.

AIMed.d52.s465.sentence: These data demonstrate loss of ligand specificity of PROTEIN0 with retained ligand dependence for receptor activation.
AIMed.d52.s465.orig_sentence: These data demonstrate loss of ligand specificity of FGFR2 with retained ligand dependence for receptor activation.

AIMed.d52.s466.sentence: These data suggest that the severe phenotypes of AS likely result from ectopic ligand-dependent activation of PROTEIN0.
AIMed.d52.s466.orig_sentence: These data suggest that the severe phenotypes of AS likely result from ectopic ligand-dependent activation of FGFR2.

AIMed.d53.s467.sentence: Structure of an extracellular PROTEIN0 cytokine receptor signaling complex.
AIMed.d53.s467.orig_sentence: Structure of an extracellular gp130 cytokine receptor signaling complex.

AIMed.d53.s468.sentence: The activation of PROTEIN0, a shared signal-transducing receptor for a family of cytokines, is initiated by recognition of ligand followed by oligomerization into a higher order signaling complex.
AIMed.d53.s468.orig_sentence: The activation of gp130, a shared signal-transducing receptor for a family of cytokines, is initiated by recognition of ligand followed by oligomerization into a higher order signaling complex.

AIMed.d53.s469.sentence: Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus encodes a functional homolog of human PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1) that activates human PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d53.s469.orig_sentence: Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus encodes a functional homolog of human interleukin-6 (IL-6) that activates human gp130.

AIMed.d53.s470.sentence: In the 2.4 angstrom crystal structure of the extracellular signaling assembly between viral PROTEIN0 and human PROTEIN1, two complexes are cross-linked into a tetramer through direct interactions between the immunoglobulin domain of PROTEIN2 and site III of viral PROTEIN3, which is necessary for receptor activation.
AIMed.d53.s470.orig_sentence: In the 2.4 angstrom crystal structure of the extracellular signaling assembly between viral IL-6 and human gp130, two complexes are cross-linked into a tetramer through direct interactions between the immunoglobulin domain of gp130 and site III of viral IL-6, which is necessary for receptor activation.

AIMed.d53.s471.sentence: Unlike human PROTEIN0 (which uses many hydrophilic residues), the viral cytokine largely uses hydrophobic amino acids to contact PROTEIN1, which enhances the complementarity of the viral PROTEIN2-PROTEIN3 binding interfaces.
AIMed.d53.s471.orig_sentence: Unlike human IL-6 (which uses many hydrophilic residues), the viral cytokine largely uses hydrophobic amino acids to contact gp130, which enhances the complementarity of the viral IL-6-gp130 binding interfaces.

AIMed.d53.s472.sentence: The cross-reactivity of PROTEIN0 is apparently due to a chemical plasticity evident in the amphipathic PROTEIN1 cytokine-binding sites.
AIMed.d53.s472.orig_sentence: The cross-reactivity of gp130 is apparently due to a chemical plasticity evident in the amphipathic gp130 cytokine-binding sites.

AIMed.d54.s473.sentence: PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1), a novel growth factor that binds to PROTEIN2 and beta receptor.
AIMed.d54.s473.orig_sentence: Platelet-derived growth factor C (PDGF-C), a novel growth factor that binds to PDGF alpha and beta receptor.

AIMed.d54.s474.sentence: We have characterized PROTEIN0, a novel growth factor belonging to the PDGF family.
AIMed.d54.s474.orig_sentence: We have characterized platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) C, a novel growth factor belonging to the PDGF family.

AIMed.d54.s475.sentence: PROTEIN0 is a multidomain protein with the N-terminal region homologous to the extracellular CUB domain of PROTEIN1, and the C-terminal region consists of a growth factor domain (GFD) with homology to vascular PROTEIN2 (25%) and PROTEIN3-chain (23%).
AIMed.d54.s475.orig_sentence: PDGF-C is a multidomain protein with the N-terminal region homologous to the extracellular CUB domain of neuropilin-1, and the C-terminal region consists of a growth factor domain (GFD) with homology to vascular endothelial growth factor (25%) and PDGF A-chain (23%).

AIMed.d54.s476.sentence: A serum-sensitive cleavage site between the two domains allows release of the GFD from the CUB domain.
AIMed.d54.s476.orig_sentence: A serum-sensitive cleavage site between the two domains allows release of the GFD from the CUB domain.

AIMed.d54.s477.sentence: Competition binding and immunoprecipitation studies on cells bearing both PROTEIN0 and beta receptors reveal a high affinity binding of recombinant GFD (PROTEIN1) to PROTEIN2 homodimers and PROTEIN3/beta heterodimers.
AIMed.d54.s477.orig_sentence: Competition binding and immunoprecipitation studies on cells bearing both PDGF alpha and beta receptors reveal a high affinity binding of recombinant GFD (PDGF-CC) to PDGF receptor-alpha homodimers and PDGF receptor-alpha/beta heterodimers.

AIMed.d54.s478.sentence: PROTEIN0 exhibits greater mitogenic potency than PROTEIN1 and comparable or greater mitogenic activity than PROTEIN2 and PROTEIN3 on several mesenchymal cell types.
AIMed.d54.s478.orig_sentence: PDGF-CC exhibits greater mitogenic potency than PDGF-AA and comparable or greater mitogenic activity than PDGF-AB and PDGF-BB on several mesenchymal cell types.

AIMed.d54.s479.sentence: Analysis of PROTEIN0 in vivo in a diabetic mouse model of delayed wound healing showed that PROTEIN1 significantly enhanced repair of a full-thickness skin excision.
AIMed.d54.s479.orig_sentence: Analysis of PDGF-CC in vivo in a diabetic mouse model of delayed wound healing showed that PDGF-CC significantly enhanced repair of a full-thickness skin excision.

AIMed.d54.s480.sentence: Together, these studies describe a third member of the PDGF family (PROTEIN0) as a potent mitogen for cells of mesenchymal origin in in vitro and in vivo systems with a binding pattern similar to PROTEIN1.
AIMed.d54.s480.orig_sentence: Together, these studies describe a third member of the PDGF family (PDGF-C) as a potent mitogen for cells of mesenchymal origin in in vitro and in vivo systems with a binding pattern similar to PDGF-AB.

AIMed.d56.s494.sentence: Cloning of PROTEIN0, a ligand for PROTEIN1 on human T cells.
AIMed.d56.s494.orig_sentence: Cloning of TRAP, a ligand for CD40 on human T cells.

AIMed.d56.s495.sentence: A cDNA clone, designated PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1) was isolated from a collection of T cell activation genes.
AIMed.d56.s495.orig_sentence: A cDNA clone, designated TRAP (TNF-related activation protein) was isolated from a collection of T cell activation genes.

AIMed.d56.s496.sentence: The polypeptide encoded by a mRNA of approx.
AIMed.d56.s496.orig_sentence: The polypeptide encoded by a mRNA of approx.

AIMed.d56.s497.sentence: 2.3 kb is 261 amino acids long with a calculated M(r) of 29.3 kDa.
AIMed.d56.s497.orig_sentence: 2.3 kb is 261 amino acids long with a calculated M(r) of 29.3 kDa.

AIMed.d56.s498.sentence: The structural features predict a type II transmembrane protein, but are also compatible with a secreted form.
AIMed.d56.s498.orig_sentence: The structural features predict a type II transmembrane protein, but are also compatible with a secreted form.

AIMed.d56.s499.sentence: PROTEIN0 is highly similar to an identified murine PROTEIN1 both at the cDNA (82.8% identity) and the protein (77.4% identity) levels, and related to tumor necrosis factor/PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d56.s499.orig_sentence: TRAP is highly similar to an identified murine CD40 ligand both at the cDNA (82.8% identity) and the protein (77.4% identity) levels, and related to tumor necrosis factor/lymphotoxin.

AIMed.d56.s500.sentence: Expressed in a murine myeloma, PROTEIN0 was identified as a ligand for PROTEIN1 by binding to a soluble PROTEIN2 construct.
AIMed.d56.s500.orig_sentence: Expressed in a murine myeloma, TRAP was identified as a ligand for CD40 by binding to a soluble CD40 construct.

AIMed.d56.s501.sentence: PROTEIN0 mRNA is expressed in a T cell-specific fashion with a maximum at 8 h after stimulation.
AIMed.d56.s501.orig_sentence: TRAP mRNA is expressed in a T cell-specific fashion with a maximum at 8 h after stimulation.

AIMed.d56.s502.sentence: The PROTEIN0 gene is located in the q26.3-q27.1 region of the X chromosome.
AIMed.d56.s502.orig_sentence: The TRAP gene is located in the q26.3-q27.1 region of the X chromosome.

AIMed.d57.s503.sentence: Reconstitution of the multiprotein complex of PROTEIN0, PROTEIN1, and PROTEIN2 in a cell-free system.
AIMed.d57.s503.orig_sentence: Reconstitution of the multiprotein complex of pp60src, hsp90, and p50 in a cell-free system.

AIMed.d57.s504.sentence: A rabbit reticulocyte lysate system that has been used to reconstitute functional complexes between steroid receptors and the 90-kDa heat shock protein (PROTEIN0) has been used here to form complexes between the PROTEIN1 tyrosine kinase and PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d57.s504.orig_sentence: A rabbit reticulocyte lysate system that has been used to reconstitute functional complexes between steroid receptors and the 90-kDa heat shock protein (hsp90) has been used here to form complexes between the pp60src tyrosine kinase and hsp90.

AIMed.d57.s505.sentence: Reticulocyte lysate forms complexes between PROTEIN0 and a temperature-sensitive mutant of Rous sarcoma virus PROTEIN1, which is normally present in cytosol virtually entirely in the multiprotein complex form.
AIMed.d57.s505.orig_sentence: Reticulocyte lysate forms complexes between hsp90 and a temperature-sensitive mutant of Rous sarcoma virus pp60v-src, which is normally present in cytosol virtually entirely in the multiprotein complex form.

AIMed.d57.s506.sentence: In addition, PROTEIN0 in the lysate complexes with wild-type PROTEIN1, of which only a small portion is normally recovered in cytosol in the native multiprotein complex, and with the cellular homolog, PROTEIN2, which has never been recovered in cytosol in the form of a native multiprotein complex with PROTEIN3.
AIMed.d57.s506.orig_sentence: In addition, hsp90 in the lysate complexes with wild-type pp60v-src, of which only a small portion is normally recovered in cytosol in the native multiprotein complex, and with the cellular homolog, pp60c-src, which has never been recovered in cytosol in the form of a native multiprotein complex with hsp90.

AIMed.d57.s507.sentence: Moreover, the reticulocyte lysate-reconstituted complex also contains the 50-kDa phosphoprotein component of the native PROTEIN0 multiprotein complex.
AIMed.d57.s507.orig_sentence: Moreover, the reticulocyte lysate-reconstituted complex also contains the 50-kDa phosphoprotein component of the native pp60v-src multiprotein complex.

AIMed.d57.s508.sentence: The native and reconstituted PROTEIN0-PROTEIN1 complexes have similar thermal stability and, like steroid receptor heterocomplexes, they are stabilized by molybdate.
AIMed.d57.s508.orig_sentence: The native and reconstituted pp60src-hsp90 complexes have similar thermal stability and, like steroid receptor heterocomplexes, they are stabilized by molybdate.

AIMed.d57.s509.sentence: As previously shown with reticulocyte lysate-reconstituted steroid receptor heteroprotein complexes, the reconstituted PROTEIN0 multiprotein complex contains PROTEIN1, which is a major candidate for providing the protein unfoldase activity required for PROTEIN2 association.
AIMed.d57.s509.orig_sentence: As previously shown with reticulocyte lysate-reconstituted steroid receptor heteroprotein complexes, the reconstituted pp60src multiprotein complex contains hsp70, which is a major candidate for providing the protein unfoldase activity required for hsp90 association.

AIMed.d58.s510.sentence: The SH2 and SH3 domain-containing protein PROTEIN0 links receptor tyrosine kinases to ras signaling.
AIMed.d58.s510.orig_sentence: The SH2 and SH3 domain-containing protein GRB2 links receptor tyrosine kinases to ras signaling.

AIMed.d58.s511.sentence: A cDNA clone encoding a novel, widely expressed protein (called PROTEIN0 or PROTEIN1) containing one src homology 2 (SH2) domain and two SH3 domains was isolated.
