AIMed.d193.s1643.sentence: The interaction was confirmed in vitro, and inside intact myogenic C2C12 cells.
AIMed.d193.s1643.orig_sentence: The interaction was confirmed in vitro, and inside intact myogenic C2C12 cells.

AIMed.d193.s1644.sentence: As expected, overexpression of either PROTEIN0/PROTEIN1 or PROTEIN2 effectively inhibited the activation of the muscle-specific PROTEIN3 promoter by the myogenic transcription factor PROTEIN4.
AIMed.d193.s1644.orig_sentence: As expected, overexpression of either Id3/HLH462 or ITF-2b effectively inhibited the activation of the muscle-specific creatine kinase promoter by the myogenic transcription factor MyoD.

AIMed.d193.s1645.sentence: However, when overexpressed simultaneously, PROTEIN0 and Id3/HLH462 counteracted each other's inhibitory effect to produce a reduced overall inhibition.
AIMed.d193.s1645.orig_sentence: However, when overexpressed simultaneously, ITF-2b and Id3/HLH462 counteracted each other's inhibitory effect to produce a reduced overall inhibition.

AIMed.d193.s1646.sentence: Moreover, while PROTEIN0 inhibited the PROTEIN1 promoter, it acted as a weak transactivator on an artificial promoter consisting of three tandem copies of the consensus myogenic factor DNA binding site.
AIMed.d193.s1646.orig_sentence: Moreover, while ITF-2b inhibited the creatine kinase promoter, it acted as a weak transactivator on an artificial promoter consisting of three tandem copies of the consensus myogenic factor DNA binding site.

AIMed.d193.s1647.sentence: Further investigation indicated that the PROTEIN0/PROTEIN1 heterodimer bound to its specific DNA binding site in vitro, and the DNA binding was effectively blocked by PROTEIN2/PROTEIN3.
AIMed.d193.s1647.orig_sentence: Further investigation indicated that the ITF-2b/MyoD heterodimer bound to its specific DNA binding site in vitro, and the DNA binding was effectively blocked by Id3/HLH462.

AIMed.d193.s1648.sentence: Additional analysis revealed the presence of transcripts for both the activating (PROTEIN0) and inhibitory (PROTEIN1) isoforms in differentiating C2C12 cultures, suggesting that both isoforms might participate in regulating the differentiation process.
AIMed.d193.s1648.orig_sentence: Additional analysis revealed the presence of transcripts for both the activating (ITF-2a) and inhibitory (ITF-2b) isoforms in differentiating C2C12 cultures, suggesting that both isoforms might participate in regulating the differentiation process.

AIMed.d193.s1649.sentence: Taken together, this study reveals a more complex pattern of regulatory interactions involving the helix-loop-helix proteins than was previously anticipated.
AIMed.d193.s1649.orig_sentence: Taken together, this study reveals a more complex pattern of regulatory interactions involving the helix-loop-helix proteins than was previously anticipated.

AIMed.d194.s1650.sentence: PROTEIN0 forms an ion channel in synthetic lipid membranes.
AIMed.d194.s1650.orig_sentence: Bcl-x(L) forms an ion channel in synthetic lipid membranes.

AIMed.d194.s1651.orig_sentence: Bcl-2-related proteins are critical regulators of cell survival that are localized to the outer mitochondrial, outer nuclear and endoplasmic reticulum membranes.

AIMed.d194.s1652.sentence: Despite their physiological importance, the biochemical function of PROTEIN0-related proteins has remained elusive.
AIMed.d194.s1652.orig_sentence: Despite their physiological importance, the biochemical function of Bcl-2-related proteins has remained elusive.

AIMed.d194.s1653.sentence: The three-dimensional structure of PROTEIN0, an inhibitor of apoptosis, was recently shown to be similar to the structures of the pore-forming domains of bacterial toxins.
AIMed.d194.s1653.orig_sentence: The three-dimensional structure of Bcl-xL, an inhibitor of apoptosis, was recently shown to be similar to the structures of the pore-forming domains of bacterial toxins.

AIMed.d194.s1654.sentence: A key feature of these pore-forming domains is the ability to form ion channels in biological membranes.
AIMed.d194.s1654.orig_sentence: A key feature of these pore-forming domains is the ability to form ion channels in biological membranes.

AIMed.d194.s1655.sentence: Here we demonstrate that PROTEIN0 shares this functional feature.
AIMed.d194.s1655.orig_sentence: Here we demonstrate that Bcl-xL shares this functional feature.

AIMed.d194.s1656.sentence: Like the bacterial toxins, PROTEIN0 can insert into either synthetic lipid vesicles or planar lipid bilayers and form an ion-conducting channel.
AIMed.d194.s1656.orig_sentence: Like the bacterial toxins, Bcl-xL can insert into either synthetic lipid vesicles or planar lipid bilayers and form an ion-conducting channel.

AIMed.d194.s1657.sentence: This channel is pH-sensitive and becomes cation-selective at physiological pH.
AIMed.d194.s1657.orig_sentence: This channel is pH-sensitive and becomes cation-selective at physiological pH.

AIMed.d194.s1658.sentence: The ion-conducting channel(s) formed by PROTEIN0 display multiple conductance states that have identical ion selectivity.
AIMed.d194.s1658.orig_sentence: The ion-conducting channel(s) formed by Bcl-xL display multiple conductance states that have identical ion selectivity.

AIMed.d194.s1659.sentence: Together, these data suggest that PROTEIN0 may maintain cell survival by regulating the permeability of the intracellular membranes to which it is distributed.
AIMed.d194.s1659.orig_sentence: Together, these data suggest that Bcl-xL may maintain cell survival by regulating the permeability of the intracellular membranes to which it is distributed.

PROTEIN1, a member of the spectrin/PROTEIN2 family of PROTEIN3-binding proteins, is identified here as a brain postsynaptic density protein that colocalizes in dendritic spines with NMDA receptors and the putative NMDA receptor-clustering molecule PROTEIN4. PROTEIN5 binds by its central rod domain to the cytoplasmic tail of both PROTEIN6 and PROTEIN7 subunits of the PROTEIN8, and can be immunoprecipitated with NMDA receptors and PROTEIN9 from rat brain.

AIMed.d195.s1663.orig_sentence: Intriguingly, NR1-alpha-actinin binding is directly antagonized by Ca2+/calmodulin.

AIMed.d195.s1664.orig_sentence: Thus alpha-actinin may play a role in both the localization of NMDA receptors and their modulation by Ca2+.

AIMed.d196.s1665.sentence: PROTEIN0 interacts with protein phosphatases PROTEIN1 and PROTEIN2 and disrupts a G2/M cell-cycle checkpoint.
AIMed.d196.s1665.orig_sentence: HOX11 interacts with protein phosphatases PP2A and PP1 and disrupts a G2/M cell-cycle checkpoint.

AIMed.d196.s1666.sentence: PROTEIN0 is an orphan homeobox gene that controls the genesis of the spleen.
AIMed.d196.s1666.orig_sentence: Hox11 is an orphan homeobox gene that controls the genesis of the spleen.

AIMed.d196.s1667.sentence: PROTEIN0 is also oncogenic, having been isolated from a chromosomal breakpoint in human T-cell leukaemia.
AIMed.d196.s1667.orig_sentence: HOX11 is also oncogenic, having been isolated from a chromosomal breakpoint in human T-cell leukaemia.

AIMed.d196.s1668.orig_sentence: Transgenic mice that redirected HOX11 to the thymus demonstrated cell-cycle aberration and progression to malignancy.

AIMed.d196.s1672.sentence: G2 arrest can be induced by gamma-irradiation, but is eliminated by expression of PROTEIN0 within a T-cell line.
AIMed.d196.s1672.orig_sentence: G2 arrest can be induced by gamma-irradiation, but is eliminated by expression of HOX11 within a T-cell line.

AIMed.d196.s1673.sentence: Thus PROTEIN0 is a cellular oncogene that targets PROTEIN1 and PROTEIN2, both of which are targets for oncogenic viruses and chemical tumour promoters.
AIMed.d196.s1673.orig_sentence: Thus HOX11 is a cellular oncogene that targets PP2A and PP1, both of which are targets for oncogenic viruses and chemical tumour promoters.

AIMed.d197.s1677.sentence: Understanding its mechanism at the amino acid level is the basis for developing small PROTEIN0-inhibiting molecules.
AIMed.d197.s1677.orig_sentence: Understanding its mechanism at the amino acid level is the basis for developing small IL-6-inhibiting molecules.

AIMed.d197.s1678.sentence: We studied the human PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1)/PROTEIN2 binding interface by a combination of molecular modelling and site-directed mutagenesis.
AIMed.d197.s1678.orig_sentence: We studied the human IL-6 (hIL-6)/hIL-6R binding interface by a combination of molecular modelling and site-directed mutagenesis.

AIMed.d197.s1680.orig_sentence: These contacts can be regarded as a hydrophobic core shielded by hydrophilic residues that are also needed for recognition.

AIMed.d197.s1681.sentence: Following this hypothesis, we altered in PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1 residues predicted to reside in the contact region and to interact with each other.
AIMed.d197.s1681.orig_sentence: Following this hypothesis, we altered in hIL-6 and hIL-6R residues predicted to reside in the contact region and to interact with each other.

AIMed.d197.s1682.sentence: We studied the capacity of these mutants to form an PROTEIN0/PROTEIN1 complex and their ability to transduce the signal.
AIMed.d197.s1682.orig_sentence: We studied the capacity of these mutants to form an IL-6/IL-6R complex and their ability to transduce the signal.

AIMed.d197.s1683.sentence: This combined approach has led to the identification of certain residue-clusters in the binding interface and to a rational explanation of their specific interactions, suggesting therein a likely mechanism of complex formation.
AIMed.d197.s1683.orig_sentence: This combined approach has led to the identification of certain residue-clusters in the binding interface and to a rational explanation of their specific interactions, suggesting therein a likely mechanism of complex formation.

AIMed.d197.s1684.sentence: The results confirm the predictive model and strongly support our hypothesis.
AIMed.d197.s1684.orig_sentence: The results confirm the predictive model and strongly support our hypothesis.

AIMed.d204.s1764.orig_sentence: This demonstrates that the C-terminal hemopexin domain of MMP-1, in contrast to the corresponding regions of gelatinase A and gelatinase B, does not interact with TIMP-1.

AIMed.d204.s1765.sentence: In summary, we have shown that the integrity of the catalytic domain of PROTEIN0 and its ability to bind Zn2+ is absolutely required for complex formation with PROTEIN1, which further underlines the importance of this region for proper regulation of enzymatic activity of PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d204.s1765.orig_sentence: In summary, we have shown that the integrity of the catalytic domain of MMP-1 and its ability to bind Zn2+ is absolutely required for complex formation with TIMP-1, which further underlines the importance of this region for proper regulation of enzymatic activity of MMP-1.

AIMed.d205.s1766.sentence: Thymocyte activation induces the association of PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1 with PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d205.s1766.orig_sentence: Thymocyte activation induces the association of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase and pp120 with CD5.

AIMed.d205.s1767.sentence: PROTEIN0 is a glycoprotein expressed on thymocytes, T cells, and a subset of B cells.
AIMed.d205.s1767.orig_sentence: CD5 is a glycoprotein expressed on thymocytes, T cells, and a subset of B cells.

AIMed.d205.s1768.sentence: Antibody-mediated cross-linking studies or studies on PROTEIN0 knockout mice implicate PROTEIN1 as a co-stimulatory or negative regulatory molecule.
AIMed.d205.s1768.orig_sentence: Antibody-mediated cross-linking studies or studies on CD5 knockout mice implicate CD5 as a co-stimulatory or negative regulatory molecule.

AIMed.d205.s1769.sentence: PROTEIN0 is rapidly phosphorylated on tyrosine (Y) residues following Tcell activation.
AIMed.d205.s1769.orig_sentence: CD5 is rapidly phosphorylated on tyrosine (Y) residues following Tcell activation.

AIMed.d205.s1770.sentence: Y429 and Y441 occur in an imperfect PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1)-like sequence.
AIMed.d205.s1770.orig_sentence: Y429 and Y441 occur in an imperfect immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motif (ITAM)-like sequence.

AIMed.d205.s1771.sentence: We investigated whether PROTEIN0, which binds to tyrosine-phosphorylated PROTEIN1, interacts with PROTEIN2 following T cell activation.
AIMed.d205.s1771.orig_sentence: We investigated whether phosphatidylinositol (PI) 3-kinase, which binds to tyrosine-phosphorylated ITAM, interacts with CD5 following T cell activation.

AIMed.d205.s1772.sentence: PROTEIN0 activity and the regulatory PROTEIN1 subunit of PROTEIN2 associated with PROTEIN3 in pervanadate-stimulated, but not in unstimulated thymocytes.
AIMed.d205.s1772.orig_sentence: PI 3-kinase activity and the regulatory p85 subunit of PI 3-kinase associated with CD5 in pervanadate-stimulated, but not in unstimulated thymocytes.

AIMed.d205.s1773.sentence: Cellular PROTEIN0 as well as the recombinant Src homology 2 (SH2) domains of PROTEIN1 bound a tyrosine-phosphorylated peptide encompassing Y463 with approximately threefold greater affinity than a doubly tyrosine-phosphorylated Y429-Y441 peptide.
AIMed.d205.s1773.orig_sentence: Cellular p85 as well as the recombinant Src homology 2 (SH2) domains of p85 bound a tyrosine-phosphorylated peptide encompassing Y463 with approximately threefold greater affinity than a doubly tyrosine-phosphorylated Y429-Y441 peptide.

AIMed.d205.s1774.sentence: Binding of the C-SH2 domain to the Y463 phosphopeptide, together with preferential binding of the N-SH2 domain to the Y429-Y441 phosphopeptide, suggests a bivalent interaction.
AIMed.d205.s1774.orig_sentence: Binding of the C-SH2 domain to the Y463 phosphopeptide, together with preferential binding of the N-SH2 domain to the Y429-Y441 phosphopeptide, suggests a bivalent interaction.

AIMed.d205.s1775.sentence: A PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1) associated with PROTEIN2 and specifically with the Y429-Y441 phosphopeptide in stimulated thymocytes.
AIMed.d205.s1775.orig_sentence: A 120-kDa phosphoprotein (pp120) associated with CD5 and specifically with the Y429-Y441 phosphopeptide in stimulated thymocytes.

AIMed.d205.s1776.sentence: We conclude that stimulation of thymocytes with pervanadate induces the recruitment of PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1 to PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d205.s1776.orig_sentence: We conclude that stimulation of thymocytes with pervanadate induces the recruitment of PI 3-kinase and pp120 to CD5.

AIMed.d206.s1777.sentence: Functional significance of PROTEIN0 association with beta 1 integrins in human epidermal keratinocytes.
AIMed.d206.s1777.orig_sentence: Functional significance of CD9 association with beta 1 integrins in human epidermal keratinocytes.

AIMed.d206.s1778.sentence: PROTEIN0 is a member of the tetraspan (TM4) family of proteins and is abundantly expressed in the epidermis.
AIMed.d206.s1778.orig_sentence: CD9 is a member of the tetraspan (TM4) family of proteins and is abundantly expressed in the epidermis.

AIMed.d206.s1779.sentence: As PROTEIN0 forms complexes with beta 1 integrins and the integrins are known to regulate keratinocyte behaviour, we investigated PROTEIN1 expression and function in human epidermal keratinocytes.
AIMed.d206.s1779.orig_sentence: As CD9 forms complexes with beta 1 integrins and the integrins are known to regulate keratinocyte behaviour, we investigated CD9 expression and function in human epidermal keratinocytes.

AIMed.d206.s1780.sentence: PROTEIN0 was present in all the living layers of the epidermis, whereas the beta 1 integrins were largely confined to the basal layer; the same relative distribution was found in stratified cultures of keratinocytes.
AIMed.d206.s1780.orig_sentence: CD9 was present in all the living layers of the epidermis, whereas the beta 1 integrins were largely confined to the basal layer; the same relative distribution was found in stratified cultures of keratinocytes.

AIMed.d206.s1781.sentence: There was extensive co-localisation of PROTEIN0 and beta 1 integrins on microvilli and at cell-cell borders of basal keratinocytes; however, in contrast to the integrins, PROTEIN1 was not found in focal adhesions.
AIMed.d206.s1781.orig_sentence: There was extensive co-localisation of CD9 and beta 1 integrins on microvilli and at cell-cell borders of basal keratinocytes; however, in contrast to the integrins, CD9 was not found in focal adhesions.

AIMed.d206.s1782.sentence: PROTEIN0 was detected in beta 1 integrin immunoprecipitates and also in immunoprecipitates of PROTEIN1 and PROTEIN2, but not of cadherins.
AIMed.d206.s1782.orig_sentence: CD9 was detected in beta 1 integrin immunoprecipitates and also in immunoprecipitates of CD44 and syndecan, but not of cadherins.

AIMed.d206.s1783.sentence: PROTEIN0 was associated with alpha 3 beta 1 but not alpha 5 beta 1; small amounts of PROTEIN1 also co-immunoprecipitated with antibodies to alpha 2 beta 1 and alpha 6 beta 4.
AIMed.d206.s1783.orig_sentence: CD9 was associated with alpha 3 beta 1 but not alpha 5 beta 1; small amounts of CD9 also co-immunoprecipitated with antibodies to alpha 2 beta 1 and alpha 6 beta 4.

AIMed.d206.s1784.sentence: Antibodies to PROTEIN0 did not affect the proportion of keratinocytes that adhered to PROTEIN1, PROTEIN2 and PROTEIN3, but did inhibit motility of keratinocytes on tissue culture plastic.
AIMed.d206.s1784.orig_sentence: Antibodies to CD9 did not affect the proportion of keratinocytes that adhered to laminin 1, type IV collagen and fibronectin, but did inhibit motility of keratinocytes on tissue culture plastic.

AIMed.d206.s1785.sentence: Like antibodies to the PROTEIN0 subunit, anti-PROTEIN1 inhibited suspension-induced terminal differentiation.
AIMed.d206.s1785.orig_sentence: Like antibodies to the beta 1 integrin subunit, anti-CD9 inhibited suspension-induced terminal differentiation.

AIMed.d206.s1786.sentence: These results suggest that PROTEIN0 may play a role in regulating keartinocyte motility and differentiation.
AIMed.d206.s1786.orig_sentence: These results suggest that CD9 may play a role in regulating keartinocyte motility and differentiation.

AIMed.d207.s1787.sentence: PROTEIN0 prevents PROTEIN1/PROTEIN2 containing PROTEIN3 complexes formation in terminally differentiated myocytes.
AIMed.d207.s1787.orig_sentence: MyoD prevents cyclinA/cdk2 containing E2F complexes formation in terminally differentiated myocytes.

AIMed.d207.s1788.sentence: Withdrawal from the cell cycle of differentiating myocytes is regulated by the PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1) protein PROTEIN2 and the pocket proteins PROTEIN3, PROTEIN4 and PROTEIN5/PROTEIN6.
AIMed.d207.s1788.orig_sentence: Withdrawal from the cell cycle of differentiating myocytes is regulated by the myogenic basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) protein MyoD and the pocket proteins pRb, p107 and pRb2/p130.

AIMed.d207.s1789.sentence: Downstream effectors of 'pocket' proteins are the components of the PROTEIN0 family of transcription factors, which regulate the G1/S-phase transition.
AIMed.d207.s1789.orig_sentence: Downstream effectors of 'pocket' proteins are the components of the E2F family of transcription factors, which regulate the G1/S-phase transition.

AIMed.d207.s1790.sentence: We analysed by EMSA the composition of PROTEIN0 complexes in cycling, quiescent undifferentiated and differentiated C2C12 skeletal muscle cells.
AIMed.d207.s1790.orig_sentence: We analysed by EMSA the composition of E2F complexes in cycling, quiescent undifferentiated and differentiated C2C12 skeletal muscle cells.

AIMed.d207.s1791.sentence: An PROTEIN0 complex containing mainly PROTEIN1 and PROTEIN2/PROTEIN3 (PROTEIN4-G0/G1 complex) appears when DNA synthesis arrests, replacing the PROTEIN5/PROTEIN6 containing PROTEIN7 complex of proliferating myoblasts (PROTEIN8-G1/S complex).
AIMed.d207.s1791.orig_sentence: An E2F complex containing mainly E2F4 and pRb2/p130 (E2F-G0/G1 complex) appears when DNA synthesis arrests, replacing the cyclinA/cdk2 containing E2F complex of proliferating myoblasts (E2F-G1/S complex).

AIMed.d207.s1792.sentence: Serum stimulation reinduces DNA synthesis and the re-appearance of PROTEIN0-G1/S complexes in quiescent myoblasts but not in differentiated C2C12 myotubes.
AIMed.d207.s1792.orig_sentence: Serum stimulation reinduces DNA synthesis and the re-appearance of E2F-G1/S complexes in quiescent myoblasts but not in differentiated C2C12 myotubes.

AIMed.d207.s1793.sentence: In differentiating C2C12 cells, PROTEIN0 complexes switch and DNA synthesis in response to serum are prevented when PROTEIN1 DNA binding activity and the cdks inhibitor PROTEIN2 downstream effector PROTEIN3 are induced.
AIMed.d207.s1793.orig_sentence: In differentiating C2C12 cells, E2F complexes switch and DNA synthesis in response to serum are prevented when MyoD DNA binding activity and the cdks inhibitor MyoD downstream effector p21 are induced.

AIMed.d207.s1794.sentence: Thus, during myogenic differentiation, formation of PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1/PROTEIN2 containing complexes is an early event, but not enough on its own to prevent the reactivation of DNA synthesis.
AIMed.d207.s1794.orig_sentence: Thus, during myogenic differentiation, formation of E2F4 and pRb2/p130 containing complexes is an early event, but not enough on its own to prevent the reactivation of DNA synthesis.

AIMed.d207.s1795.sentence: Using a subclone of C3H10T1/2 mouse fibroblasts stably expressing PROTEIN0-PROTEIN1 (PROTEIN2-PROTEIN3) chimerae, we found that estrogen directed PROTEIN4 activation prevents the reassociation of PROTEIN5/PROTEIN6 to the PROTEIN7 containing complex following serum stimulation and this correlates with suppression of PROTEIN8 activity and the inability of cells to re-enter the cell cycle.
AIMed.d207.s1795.orig_sentence: Using a subclone of C3H10T1/2 mouse fibroblasts stably expressing Estrogen Receptor-MyoD (ER-MyoD) chimerae, we found that estrogen directed MyoD activation prevents the reassociation of cyclinA/cdk2 to the E2F4 containing complex following serum stimulation and this correlates with suppression of E2F activity and the inability of cells to re-enter the cell cycle.

AIMed.d207.s1796.sentence: Our data indicate that, in differentiating myocytes, one mechanism through which PROTEIN0 induces permanent cell cycle arrest involves PROTEIN1 upregulation and suppression of the proliferation-associated cdks-containing PROTEIN2 complexes formation.
AIMed.d207.s1796.orig_sentence: Our data indicate that, in differentiating myocytes, one mechanism through which MyoD induces permanent cell cycle arrest involves p21 upregulation and suppression of the proliferation-associated cdks-containing E2F complexes formation.

AIMed.d208.s1797.sentence: Early events in TNF signaling: a story of associations and dissociations.
AIMed.d208.s1797.orig_sentence: Early events in TNF signaling: a story of associations and dissociations.

AIMed.d208.s1798.sentence: At the cellular level, the multifunctional cytokine tumor necrosis factor (TNF) modulates growth and activates genes through various intermediates, including protein kinases, protein phosphatases, reactive oxygen intermediates, phospholipases, proteases, sphingomyelinases, and transcription factors.
AIMed.d208.s1798.orig_sentence: At the cellular level, the multifunctional cytokine tumor necrosis factor (TNF) modulates growth and activates genes through various intermediates, including protein kinases, protein phosphatases, reactive oxygen intermediates, phospholipases, proteases, sphingomyelinases, and transcription factors.

AIMed.d208.s1799.sentence: Unlike many cytokine receptors, however, the cytoplasmic domain (CD) of the TNF receptors lacks an intrinsic protein kinase activity and yet on interaction with ligand it phosphorylates various proteins.
AIMed.d208.s1799.orig_sentence: Unlike many cytokine receptors, however, the cytoplasmic domain (CD) of the TNF receptors lacks an intrinsic protein kinase activity and yet on interaction with ligand it phosphorylates various proteins.

AIMed.d208.s1800.sentence: Although the kinetics of most of these activities differ, their interactions are coordinated through the selective interplay between the CD of the receptors and the associated proteins.
AIMed.d208.s1800.orig_sentence: Although the kinetics of most of these activities differ, their interactions are coordinated through the selective interplay between the CD of the receptors and the associated proteins.

AIMed.d208.s1801.sentence: A unique pathway has been identified by the ability of the TNF receptors to associate with a novel family of proteins.
AIMed.d208.s1801.orig_sentence: A unique pathway has been identified by the ability of the TNF receptors to associate with a novel family of proteins.

AIMed.d208.s1802.sentence: Two distinct families of proteins have emerged, the TNF receptor-associated factors (TRAFs) and the death domain homologues.
AIMed.d208.s1802.orig_sentence: Two distinct families of proteins have emerged, the TNF receptor-associated factors (TRAFs) and the death domain homologues.

AIMed.d208.s1803.sentence: The cloning of members of these gene families and the identification of the protein-interaction motifs found within their gene products has initiated the molecular identity of factors (PROTEIN0, PROTEIN1/PROTEIN2, PROTEIN3, PROTEIN4/PROTEIN5, and TRAFs) associated with both of the PROTEIN6 and PROTEIN7 forms of the TNF receptor and with other members of the TNF receptor superfamily.
AIMed.d208.s1803.orig_sentence: The cloning of members of these gene families and the identification of the protein-interaction motifs found within their gene products has initiated the molecular identity of factors (TRADD, FADD/MORT, RIP, FLICE/MACH, and TRAFs) associated with both of the p60 and p80 forms of the TNF receptor and with other members of the TNF receptor superfamily.

AIMed.d208.s1804.sentence: In this review, we summarize these and other TNF receptor-associated proteins and their potential roles in regulating the activation of PROTEIN0 and apoptosis, two major responses activated by engagement of TNF receptors by the ligand.
AIMed.d208.s1804.orig_sentence: In this review, we summarize these and other TNF receptor-associated proteins and their potential roles in regulating the activation of nuclear factor-kappaB and apoptosis, two major responses activated by engagement of TNF receptors by the ligand.

AIMed.d209.s1805.sentence: Protein binding and signaling properties of PROTEIN0 suggest a unique effector function.
AIMed.d209.s1805.orig_sentence: Protein binding and signaling properties of RIN1 suggest a unique effector function.

AIMed.d209.s1806.sentence: Human PROTEIN0 was first characterized as a PROTEIN1 PROTEIN2 based on the properties of its carboxyl-terminal domain.
AIMed.d209.s1806.orig_sentence: Human RIN1 was first characterized as a RAS binding protein based on the properties of its carboxyl-terminal domain.

AIMed.d209.s1807.sentence: We now show that full-length PROTEIN0 interacts with activated PROTEIN1 in mammalian cells and defines a minimum region of 434 aa required for efficient PROTEIN2 binding.
AIMed.d209.s1807.orig_sentence: We now show that full-length RIN1 interacts with activated RAS in mammalian cells and defines a minimum region of 434 aa required for efficient RAS binding.

AIMed.d209.s1808.sentence: PROTEIN0 interacts with the "effector domain" of PROTEIN1 and employs some PROTEIN2 determinants that are common to, and others that are distinct from, those required for the binding of PROTEIN3, a known PROTEIN4 effector.
AIMed.d209.s1808.orig_sentence: RIN1 interacts with the "effector domain" of RAS and employs some RAS determinants that are common to, and others that are distinct from, those required for the binding of RAF1, a known RAS effector.

AIMed.d209.s1809.sentence: The same domain of PROTEIN0 that binds PROTEIN1 also interacts with 14-3-3 proteins, extending the similarity between PROTEIN2 and other PROTEIN3 effectors.
AIMed.d209.s1809.orig_sentence: The same domain of RIN1 that binds RAS also interacts with 14-3-3 proteins, extending the similarity between RIN1 and other RAS effectors.

AIMed.d209.s1810.sentence: When expressed in mammalian cells, the PROTEIN0 binding domain of PROTEIN1 can act as a dominant negative signal transduction blocker.
AIMed.d209.s1810.orig_sentence: When expressed in mammalian cells, the RAS binding domain of RIN1 can act as a dominant negative signal transduction blocker.

AIMed.d209.s1811.sentence: The amino-terminal domain of PROTEIN0 contains a proline-rich sequence similar to consensus Src homology 3 (SH3) binding regions.
AIMed.d209.s1811.orig_sentence: The amino-terminal domain of RIN1 contains a proline-rich sequence similar to consensus Src homology 3 (SH3) binding regions.

AIMed.d209.s1812.sentence: This PROTEIN0 sequence shows preferential binding to the PROTEIN1 domain in vitro.
AIMed.d209.s1812.orig_sentence: This RIN1 sequence shows preferential binding to the ABL-SH3 domain in vitro.

AIMed.d209.s1813.sentence: Moreover, the amino-terminal domain of PROTEIN0 directly associates with, and is tyrosine phosphorylated by, PROTEIN1.
AIMed.d209.s1813.orig_sentence: Moreover, the amino-terminal domain of RIN1 directly associates with, and is tyrosine phosphorylated by, c-ABL.

AIMed.d209.s1814.sentence: In addition, PROTEIN0 encodes a functional SH2 domain that has the potential to activate downstream signals.
AIMed.d209.s1814.orig_sentence: In addition, RIN1 encodes a functional SH2 domain that has the potential to activate downstream signals.

AIMed.d209.s1815.sentence: These data suggest that PROTEIN0 is able to mediate multiple signals.
AIMed.d209.s1815.orig_sentence: These data suggest that RIN1 is able to mediate multiple signals.

AIMed.d209.s1816.sentence: A differential pattern of expression and alternate splicing indicate several levels of PROTEIN0 regulation.
AIMed.d209.s1816.orig_sentence: A differential pattern of expression and alternate splicing indicate several levels of RIN1 regulation.

AIMed.d211.s1827.sentence: Ligands for ErbB-family receptors encoded by a neuregulin-like gene.
AIMed.d211.s1827.orig_sentence: Ligands for ErbB-family receptors encoded by a neuregulin-like gene.

AIMed.d211.s1828.sentence: Neuregulins (also called ARIA, GGF, heregulin or NDF) are a group of polypeptide factors that arise from alternative RNA splicing of a single gene.
AIMed.d211.s1828.orig_sentence: Neuregulins (also called ARIA, GGF, heregulin or NDF) are a group of polypeptide factors that arise from alternative RNA splicing of a single gene.

AIMed.d211.s1829.sentence: Through their interaction with the ErbB family of receptors (PROTEIN0, PROTEIN1 and PROTEIN2), neuregulins help to regulate cell growth and differentiation in many tissues.
AIMed.d211.s1829.orig_sentence: Through their interaction with the ErbB family of receptors (ErbB2, ErbB3 and ErbB4), neuregulins help to regulate cell growth and differentiation in many tissues.

AIMed.d211.s1830.sentence: Here we report the cloning of a second neuregulin-like gene, PROTEIN0.
AIMed.d211.s1830.orig_sentence: Here we report the cloning of a second neuregulin-like gene, neuregulin-2.

AIMed.d211.s1831.sentence: The encoded product of the PROTEIN0 gene has a motif structure similar to that of neuregulins and an alternative splicing site in the PROTEIN1(PROTEIN2)-like domain gives rise to two isoforms (alpha and beta).
AIMed.d211.s1831.orig_sentence: The encoded product of the neuregulin-2 gene has a motif structure similar to that of neuregulins and an alternative splicing site in the epidermal growth factor(EGF)-like domain gives rise to two isoforms (alpha and beta).

AIMed.d211.s1832.sentence: Northern blot and in situ hybridization analysis of adult rat tissues indicate that expression of PROTEIN0 is highest in the cerebellum, and the expression pattern is different from that of neuregulins.
AIMed.d211.s1832.orig_sentence: Northern blot and in situ hybridization analysis of adult rat tissues indicate that expression of neuregulin-2 is highest in the cerebellum, and the expression pattern is different from that of neuregulins.

AIMed.d211.s1833.sentence: Recombinant PROTEIN0 induces the tyrosine-phosphorylation of PROTEIN1, PROTEIN2 and PROTEIN3 in cell lines expressing all of these ErbB-family receptors.
AIMed.d211.s1833.orig_sentence: Recombinant neuregulin-2beta induces the tyrosine-phosphorylation of ErbB2, ErbB3 and ErbB4 in cell lines expressing all of these ErbB-family receptors.

AIMed.d211.s1834.sentence: However, in cell lines with defined combinations of ErbBs, PROTEIN0 only activates those with PROTEIN1 and/or PROTEIN2, suggesting that signalling by PROTEIN3 is mediated by PROTEIN4 and/or PROTEIN5 receptors.
AIMed.d211.s1834.orig_sentence: However, in cell lines with defined combinations of ErbBs, neuregulin-2beta only activates those with ErbB3 and/or ErbB4, suggesting that signalling by neuregulin-2 is mediated by ErbB3 and/or ErbB4 receptors.

AIMed.d213.s1843.sentence: Multiple mechanisms of transcriptional repression by PROTEIN0.
AIMed.d213.s1843.orig_sentence: Multiple mechanisms of transcriptional repression by YY1.

AIMed.d213.s1844.sentence: The four C-terminal GLI-Kruppel type zinc fingers of PROTEIN0 have been identified as a transcriptional repression domain.
AIMed.d213.s1844.orig_sentence: The four C-terminal GLI-Kruppel type zinc fingers of YY1 have been identified as a transcriptional repression domain.

AIMed.d213.s1845.sentence: Previous reports have proposed DNA-bending and activator-quenching mechanisms for this zinc finger-mediated repression.
AIMed.d213.s1845.orig_sentence: Previous reports have proposed DNA-bending and activator-quenching mechanisms for this zinc finger-mediated repression.

AIMed.d213.s1846.sentence: In addition, previous work indicated that PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1 might be involved in PROTEIN2-mediated repression.
AIMed.d213.s1846.orig_sentence: In addition, previous work indicated that p300 and CBP might be involved in YY1-mediated repression.

AIMed.d213.s1847.sentence: We have analyzed these possible models for the zinc finger-mediated repression.
AIMed.d213.s1847.orig_sentence: We have analyzed these possible models for the zinc finger-mediated repression.

AIMed.d213.s1848.sentence: The role of each zinc finger in the repression and DNA-binding functions was determined by using a structure-and-function approach.
AIMed.d213.s1848.orig_sentence: The role of each zinc finger in the repression and DNA-binding functions was determined by using a structure-and-function approach.

AIMed.d213.s1849.sentence: We show that zinc finger 2 of PROTEIN0 plays a central role in both DNA binding and transcriptional repression.
AIMed.d213.s1849.orig_sentence: We show that zinc finger 2 of YY1 plays a central role in both DNA binding and transcriptional repression.

AIMed.d213.s1850.sentence: However, a survey of a panel of PROTEIN0 mutants indicates that these two functions can be separated, which argues against the DNA-bending model for repression.
AIMed.d213.s1850.orig_sentence: However, a survey of a panel of YY1 mutants indicates that these two functions can be separated, which argues against the DNA-bending model for repression.

AIMed.d213.s1851.sentence: We show that the physical interaction between PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1, a coactivator for PROTEIN2, is not sufficient for repression of PROTEIN3-mediated transcription.
AIMed.d213.s1851.orig_sentence: We show that the physical interaction between YY1 and p300, a coactivator for CREB, is not sufficient for repression of CREB-mediated transcription.

AIMed.d213.s1852.sentence: Our studies indicate that PROTEIN0 functions as an activator-specific repressor.
AIMed.d213.s1852.orig_sentence: Our studies indicate that YY1 functions as an activator-specific repressor.

AIMed.d213.s1853.sentence: Repression of PROTEIN0-directed transcription may be accomplished through direct physical interaction between PROTEIN1 and this activator.
AIMed.d213.s1853.orig_sentence: Repression of CTF-1-directed transcription may be accomplished through direct physical interaction between YY1 and this activator.

AIMed.d213.s1854.sentence: In contrast, physical interaction is not necessary for PROTEIN0 to repress PROTEIN1- and PROTEIN2-mediated transcription.
AIMed.d213.s1854.orig_sentence: In contrast, physical interaction is not necessary for YY1 to repress Sp1- and CREB-mediated transcription.

AIMed.d213.s1855.sentence: Rather, the repression likely reflects an ability of PROTEIN0 to interfere with communication between these activators and their targets within the general transcription machinery.
AIMed.d213.s1855.orig_sentence: Rather, the repression likely reflects an ability of YY1 to interfere with communication between these activators and their targets within the general transcription machinery.

AIMed.d213.s1856.sentence: Taken together, our results suggest that PROTEIN0 employs multiple mechanisms to achieve activator-specific repression.
AIMed.d213.s1856.orig_sentence: Taken together, our results suggest that YY1 employs multiple mechanisms to achieve activator-specific repression.

AIMed.d214.s1857.sentence: Proto-oncoprotein PROTEIN0 interacts with PROTEIN1 in activated thymocytes and peripheral T cells.
AIMed.d214.s1857.orig_sentence: Proto-oncoprotein Vav interacts with c-Cbl in activated thymocytes and peripheral T cells.

AIMed.d214.s1858.sentence: The molecular adapter PROTEIN0 is rapidly tyrosine phosphorylated following stimulation through the PROTEIN1 and associates with PROTEIN2 homology domain-2 (SH2)/SH3 domain-containing adapters such as PROTEIN3, PROTEIN4, and PROTEIN5, which interact with guanine nucleotide exchange factors specific for the Ras family.
AIMed.d214.s1858.orig_sentence: The molecular adapter c-Cbl is rapidly tyrosine phosphorylated following stimulation through the TCR and associates with Src homology domain-2 (SH2)/SH3 domain-containing adapters such as Grb2, Crk, and Crk-L, which interact with guanine nucleotide exchange factors specific for the Ras family.

AIMed.d214.s1859.sentence: This suggests that PROTEIN0 may link PROTEIN1 activation to molecules that regulate GTP binding proteins.
AIMed.d214.s1859.orig_sentence: This suggests that c-Cbl may link TCR activation to molecules that regulate GTP binding proteins.

AIMed.d214.s1860.sentence: The SH2/SH3-containing protein PROTEIN0 also contains a guanine nucleotide exchange factor domain, and PROTEIN1 has a crucial role in thymocyte development and activation of peripheral T cells following stimulation through the PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d214.s1860.orig_sentence: The SH2/SH3-containing protein Vav also contains a guanine nucleotide exchange factor domain, and Vav has a crucial role in thymocyte development and activation of peripheral T cells following stimulation through the TCR.

AIMed.d214.s1861.sentence: Here we show that PROTEIN0 and PROTEIN1 form inducible molecular complexes in PROTEIN2-activated murine thymocytes and peripheral T cells as well as pervanadate-treated T cells.
AIMed.d214.s1861.orig_sentence: Here we show that Vav and c-Cbl form inducible molecular complexes in TCR-activated murine thymocytes and peripheral T cells as well as pervanadate-treated T cells.

AIMed.d214.s1862.sentence: PROTEIN0/PROTEIN1 interactions are also detectable in freshly isolated T cells from gene-targeted mice that lack the T cell-specific inhibitory receptor PROTEIN2, in which PROTEIN3 is hyperphosphorylated on tyrosine residues.

AIMed.d217.s1884.orig_sentence: The F275L mutant, mimicking the loss of function murine gld mutation, exhibited a high propensity for aggregation and was unable to bind to Fas.

AIMed.d217.s1887.orig_sentence: Interestingly, mutant Y218F could induce apoptosis in murine, but not human cells.

AIMed.d218.s1889.sentence: PROTEIN0 (PROTEIN1) is a hematopoietin important for megakaryocyte proliferation and production of blood platelets.
AIMed.d218.s1889.orig_sentence: Thrombopoietin (TPO) is a hematopoietin important for megakaryocyte proliferation and production of blood platelets.

AIMed.d218.s1890.orig_sentence: We sought to characterize how TPO binds and activates its receptor, myeloproliferative leukemia virus receptor.

AIMed.d218.s1891.sentence: The PROTEIN0-like domain of PROTEIN1 (TPO1-153) has been fused to the PROTEIN2 coat protein of M13 bacteriophage.
AIMed.d218.s1891.orig_sentence: The erythropoietin-like domain of TPO (TPO1-153) has been fused to the gIII coat protein of M13 bacteriophage.

AIMed.d218.s1898.orig_sentence: These results suggest that TPO has two distinct receptor-binding sites that function to dimerize TPO receptors in a sequential fashion.

AIMed.d219.s1899.sentence: PROTEIN0 negatively regulates PROTEIN1 activity by interactions with the PROTEIN2 cysteine-rich domain.
AIMed.d219.s1899.orig_sentence: 14-3-3 zeta negatively regulates raf-1 activity by interactions with the Raf-1 cysteine-rich domain.

AIMed.d219.s1900.sentence: Although PROTEIN0 is a critical effector of PROTEIN1 signaling and transformation, the mechanism by which PROTEIN2 promotes PROTEIN3 activation is complex and remains poorly understood.
AIMed.d219.s1900.orig_sentence: Although Raf-1 is a critical effector of Ras signaling and transformation, the mechanism by which Ras promotes Raf-1 activation is complex and remains poorly understood.

AIMed.d219.s1901.sentence: We recently reported that PROTEIN0 interaction with the PROTEIN1 PROTEIN2 (PROTEIN3, residues 139-184) may be required for PROTEIN4 activation.
AIMed.d219.s1901.orig_sentence: We recently reported that Ras interaction with the Raf-1 cysteine-rich domain (Raf-CRD, residues 139-184) may be required for Raf-1 activation.

AIMed.d219.s1902.sentence: The PROTEIN0 is located in the NH2-terminal negative regulatory domain of PROTEIN1 and is highly homologous to cysteine-rich domains found in protein kinase C family members.
AIMed.d219.s1902.orig_sentence: The Raf-CRD is located in the NH2-terminal negative regulatory domain of Raf-1 and is highly homologous to cysteine-rich domains found in protein kinase C family members.

AIMed.d219.s1903.sentence: Recent studies indicate that the structural integrity of the PROTEIN0 is also critical for PROTEIN1 interaction with 14-3-3 proteins.
AIMed.d219.s1903.orig_sentence: Recent studies indicate that the structural integrity of the Raf-CRD is also critical for Raf-1 interaction with 14-3-3 proteins.

AIMed.d219.s1904.sentence: However, whether 14-3-3 proteins interact directly with the PROTEIN0 and how this interaction may mediate PROTEIN1 function has not been determined.
AIMed.d219.s1904.orig_sentence: However, whether 14-3-3 proteins interact directly with the Raf-CRD and how this interaction may mediate Raf-1 function has not been determined.

AIMed.d219.s1906.sentence: Moreover, mutation of PROTEIN0 residues 143-145 impairs binding of 14-3-3, but not PROTEIN1, to the PROTEIN2.
AIMed.d219.s1906.orig_sentence: Moreover, mutation of Raf-1 residues 143-145 impairs binding of 14-3-3, but not Ras, to the Raf-CRD.

AIMed.d219.s1907.orig_sentence: Introduction of mutations that impair 14-3-3 binding resulted in full-length Raf-1 mutants with enhanced transforming activity.

AIMed.d219.s1908.sentence: Thus, 14-3-3 interaction with the PROTEIN0 may serve in negative regulation of PROTEIN1 function by facilitating dissociation of 14-3-3 from the NH2 terminus of PROTEIN2 to promote subsequent events necessary for full activation of PROTEIN3.

AIMed.d220.s1909.orig_sentence: Interactions between brain-derived neurotrophic factor and the TRKB receptor. Identification of two ligand binding domains in soluble TRKB by affinity separation and chemical cross-linking.

AIMed.d220.s1910.orig_sentence: The extracellular domain of the human neurotrophin TRKB receptor expressed in Chinese hamster ovary cells is a highly glycosylated protein, possessing binding ability for brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF).

AIMed.d220.s1911.sentence: Two distinct ligand binding domains of PROTEIN0 were isolated from proteolytic digests of the receptor by affinity separation on immobilized PROTEIN1.
AIMed.d220.s1911.orig_sentence: Two distinct ligand binding domains of TRKB were isolated from proteolytic digests of the receptor by affinity separation on immobilized BDNF.

AIMed.d220.s1912.sentence: One of these domains consists of amino acid residues 103-181 and contains both the third leucine-rich motif and the second cysteine cluster domain.
AIMed.d220.s1912.orig_sentence: One of these domains consists of amino acid residues 103-181 and contains both the third leucine-rich motif and the second cysteine cluster domain.

AIMed.d220.s1913.sentence: The second domain is close to the second immunoglobulin-like domain (amino acid residues 342-394).
AIMed.d220.s1913.orig_sentence: The second domain is close to the second immunoglobulin-like domain (amino acid residues 342-394).

AIMed.d220.s1914.sentence: Each of these two domains can bind PROTEIN0 independently.

AIMed.d220.s1915.sentence: Disulfide linkages present in the first domain are necessary for PROTEIN0 binding, probably because of preservation of the native conformation.

AIMed.d220.s1918.sentence: Several synthetic peptides corresponding to amino acid residues 343-379 were able to bind immobilized PROTEIN0.
AIMed.d220.s1918.orig_sentence: Several synthetic peptides corresponding to amino acid residues 343-379 were able to bind immobilized BDNF.

AIMed.d220.s1919.sentence: Amino acid substitution and cross-linking analysis indicated that amino acids Phe347, Asp354, and Tyr361 are intimately involved in PROTEIN0 binding.
AIMed.d220.s1919.orig_sentence: Amino acid substitution and cross-linking analysis indicated that amino acids Phe347, Asp354, and Tyr361 are intimately involved in BDNF binding.

AIMed.d220.s1920.sentence: These results, obtained from a variety of experimental techniques, highlight the importance of two distinct regions of the extracellular domain of the PROTEIN0 PROTEIN1 in binding PROTEIN2.

AIMed.d222.s1927.sentence: A PROTEIN0 yeast two hybrid screen reveals interactions with 14-3-3 isoforms and cytoskeletal components.
AIMed.d222.s1927.orig_sentence: A c-Cbl yeast two hybrid screen reveals interactions with 14-3-3 isoforms and cytoskeletal components.

AIMed.d222.s1928.sentence: The protein product of PROTEIN0 proto-oncogene is known to interact with several proteins, including PROTEIN1, PROTEIN2 and PROTEIN3, and is thought to regulate signalling by many cell surface receptors.
AIMed.d222.s1928.orig_sentence: The protein product of c-cbl proto-oncogene is known to interact with several proteins, including Grb2, Crk and PI3 kinase, and is thought to regulate signalling by many cell surface receptors.

AIMed.d222.s1929.orig_sentence: The precise function of c-Cbl in these pathways is not clear, although a genetic analysis in Caenorhabditis elegans suggests that c-Cbl is a negative regulator of the epidermal growth factor receptor.

AIMed.d222.s1930.sentence: Here we describe a yeast two hybrid screen performed with PROTEIN0 in an attempt to further elucidate its role in signal transduction.
AIMed.d222.s1930.orig_sentence: Here we describe a yeast two hybrid screen performed with c-Cbl in an attempt to further elucidate its role in signal transduction.

AIMed.d222.s1931.orig_sentence: The screen identified interactions involving c-Cbl and two 14-3-3 isoforms, cytokeratin 18, human unconventional myosin IC, and a recently identified SH3 domain containing protein, SH3 P17.

AIMed.d222.s1932.orig_sentence: We have used the yeast two hybrid assay to localise regions of c-Cbl required for its interaction with each of the proteins.

AIMed.d224.s1945.sentence: PROTEIN0- and PROTEIN1-dependent PROTEIN2 surface expression correlates with the binding of an MHC class I leader peptide.
AIMed.d224.s1945.orig_sentence: TAP- and tapasin-dependent HLA-E surface expression correlates with the binding of an MHC class I leader peptide.

AIMed.d224.s1946.sentence: BACKGROUND: The human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class lb molecule PROTEIN0 is transcribed in most tissues but little is known about its localisation within the cell.
AIMed.d224.s1946.orig_sentence: BACKGROUND: The human major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class lb molecule HLA-E is transcribed in most tissues but little is known about its localisation within the cell.

AIMed.d224.s1947.sentence: We have recently shown that PROTEIN0 binds signal-sequence-derived peptides from human MHC class I molecules in vitro.
AIMed.d224.s1947.orig_sentence: We have recently shown that HLA-E binds signal-sequence-derived peptides from human MHC class I molecules in vitro.

AIMed.d224.s1948.sentence: RESULTS: Using a newly characterised antibody recognising HLA-E, we show that PROTEIN0 is expressed at the cell surface.
AIMed.d224.s1948.orig_sentence: RESULTS: Using a newly characterised antibody recognising HLA-E, we show that HLA-E is expressed at the cell surface.

AIMed.d224.s1949.sentence: We demonstrate that PROTEIN0 surface expression is correlated with the presence of MHC class I molecules which provide suitable leader sequence peptides capable of binding to PROTEIN1.
AIMed.d224.s1949.orig_sentence: We demonstrate that HLA-E surface expression is correlated with the presence of MHC class I molecules which provide suitable leader sequence peptides capable of binding to HLA-E.

AIMed.d224.s1950.sentence: Further studies on the interaction of PROTEIN0 with molecules in the endoplasmic reticulum revealed that PROTEIN1 associates with the PROTEIN2 (PROTEIN3) and PROTEIN4, and that PROTEIN5 expression is PROTEIN6-dependent and tapasin-dependent.
AIMed.d224.s1950.orig_sentence: Further studies on the interaction of HLA-E with molecules in the endoplasmic reticulum revealed that HLA-E associates with the transporter associated with antigen processing (TAP) and calreticulin, and that HLA-E expression is TAP-dependent and tapasin-dependent.

AIMed.d224.s1951.sentence: In addition, PROTEIN0 dissociates from PROTEIN1 upon binding of MHC class I leader sequence peptides.
AIMed.d224.s1951.orig_sentence: In addition, HLA-E dissociates from TAP upon binding of MHC class I leader sequence peptides.

AIMed.d224.s1952.sentence: CONCLUSION: These experiments establish that surface expression of PROTEIN0 is regulated by the binding of a restricted pool of peptides from the leader sequence of MHC class I molecules.
AIMed.d224.s1952.orig_sentence: CONCLUSION: These experiments establish that surface expression of HLA-E is regulated by the binding of a restricted pool of peptides from the leader sequence of MHC class I molecules.

AIMed.d224.s1953.sentence: The correlation between PROTEIN0 and MHC class I surface expression might be relevant to the function of PROTEIN1.
AIMed.d224.s1953.orig_sentence: The correlation between HLA-E and MHC class I surface expression might be relevant to the function of HLA-E.

AIMed.d224.s1954.sentence: Our results also show that, although these PROTEIN0 binding peptides are derived from signal sequences, they may be released back into the cytosol and subsequently translocated by the PROTEIN1 complex and loaded onto PROTEIN2 molecules.
AIMed.d224.s1954.orig_sentence: Our results also show that, although these HLA-E binding peptides are derived from signal sequences, they may be released back into the cytosol and subsequently translocated by the TAP complex and loaded onto HLA-E molecules.
